articles.title: P866.38 million in flood control funds returned to treasury --DOJ
articles.summary: The Department of Justice (DOJ) on Thursday said that P866.38 million worth of flood control funds have been returned to the country"s coffers as of October.

blocks.text: Published November 12, 2026 7:45pm
The Department of Justice (DOJ) on Thursday said that P866.38 million worth of flood control funds have been returned to the country’s coffers as of October.

In a press briefing, DOJ Undersecretary Raul Vasquez presented several highlights of the agency’s performance for the year 2026. One of these agency’s highlights included its handling of the multi-billion flood control scam.
“The department has handled 29 cases, and as of October 2026, P866,381,500 has been returned to the DOJ and deposited with the Bureau of Treasury,” Vasquez said.

Vasquez later clarified that the amount solely came from the proponents of the Bulacan case. The flood control scam was initially exposed in Bulacan First District Engineering Office, where several former employees have admitted to funneling money into bogus flood control projects.

The DOJ has since named a number of individuals from the Bulacan case as a protected witness. Vasquez said that there is a continuing offer for people to become a witness as long as they return stolen funds, but clarified that the agency has no specific quota.

“The goal is not just P1 billion because of the continuing efforts to require the restitution of public funds that were unlawfully acquired by certain individuals as a precondition to their being accepted into the witness protection program,” Vasquez said.

“It is an open ended measure that we will continue to uphold, that there is an open opportunity for those who are charged to restore whatever it is that they got unlawfully and be admitted in the Witness Protection Program and be granted certain benefits that would be good for them and their families. So there is no set amount,” he added.

According to DOJ Undersecretary Deo Marco, dismissed Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) engineer Henry Alcantara was the last to return stolen funds. Former DPWH Undersecretary Roberto Bernardo’s restitution is ongoing, as some of those being returned are properties.

For flood control cases, Vasquez said that three malversation and graft cases have been filed before RegionalTrial Courts, five tax cases were filed before the Court of Tax Appeals, and two cases were endorsed to the Ombudsman. The DOJ has also dismissed eight tax-related cases.
Vasquez stressed that it was their responsibility to ensure that all the allegations are subject to proper legal processes. —NB, GMA News

articles.title: BIR chief Mendoza goes to Customs, DOF usec Ligon is new tax chief
articles.summary: The BIR continues to face extortion complaints while the Customs bureau is trying to address port congestion and other issues

blocks.text: Charlito Mendoza (left) and Rolando Ligon Jr.
Rappler file; PEZA FB
The BIR continues to face extortion complaints while the Customs bureau is trying to address port congestion and other issues

MANILA, Philippines – President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. reshuffled the heads of the government’s top two revenue agencies, his third major leadership shakeup of these Department of Finance (DOF) offices since assuming the presidency in mid-2022.

In a statement on Thursday, November 12, Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) Commissioner Charlito Mendoza confirmed that he is moving to the Bureau of Customs (BOC) replacing Commissioner Ariel Nepomuceno.

“I look forward to working with the men and women of the BOC to carry out the priorities of President Marcos Jr. and [Finance] Secretary [Frederick] Go — strengthening border protection, sustaining revenue collection, and facilitating legitimate trade. We have important work ahead of us, and I am ready to get started,” he said.
Mendoza held the top BIR post for a year after Marcos appointed him on November 13, 2025.

The BIR continues to face complaints about corruption. Last September, a Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PCCI) officer testified before a Senate committee on trade, commerce, and entrepreneurship that BIR examiners were still extorting businesses via letters of authority (LOAs) and asking for illicit deals in exchange for tax settlements. Prior to that exposé, the BIR had vowed reforms in the LOA system. (READ: [Ask the Tax Whiz] Why is the BIR auditing your business?)

blocks.caption: BIR suspends field audits amid calls to probe alleged extortion scheme

blocks.text: Finance Undersecretary Rolando Ligon Jr. replaces Mendoza in the BIR. As undersecretary, Ligon supervised the BIR and the Customs bureau. Ligon is the third BIR chief under the Marcos administration. Romeo Lumagui Jr. was Marcos’ first BIR commissioner and served from July 2022 to November 2025.

Ligon, more specifically, was the supervising finance undersecretary that handled the DOF’s Revenue Integrity Protection Service or RIPS. RIPS is officially described as the “anti-corruption arm of the DOF,” which investigates allegations of corruption in the BIR, Customs, and other finance-attached offices. If warranted, RIPS then files charges against erring public servants.

Ligon was a tax lawyer for the Campos, Canobas, Sy, Selva, Ligon & Dato Law from 2018 to 2025, and is a part-time professor for law on taxation at the Lyceum of the Philippines University, according to his LinkedIn account.

blocks.caption: PORT CONGESTION. Customs Commissioner Ariel Nepomuceno and other officials join a meeting led by Finance Secretary Frederick Go on addressing port congestion and other stakeholder concerns, on November 11, 2026. Photo courtesy of Department of Finance FB

blocks.text: From the Customs bureau, Nepomuceno will now head the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA), replacing its president and CEO Joshua Bingcang.
Bingcang, an engineer, is moving to the Philippine Export Zone Authority or PEZA, the country’s second largest investment promotion agency, Secretary Go announced on Thursday.

Nepomuceno was appointed Customs chief only in June 2025. This new post marks his third under the Marcos administration. He has been trying to address complaints from the business community about port congestion, which is delaying the release of goods, particulary in the port of Manila.

According to the DOF, among the agreed measures in a meeting this week are the expansion of container-yard capacity and faster withdrawal of overstaying laden containers. The Customs bureau reported that 45% of these containers had been cleared as of Monday, November 9.

Prior to being Customs chief, Nepomuceno served as administrator of the Office of Civil Defense under the Department of National Defense from December 2022 to June 2025. He held various posts in the Customs bureau during the Rodrigo Duterte administration.

The BCDA has been in the news lately as the Marcos administration does the finishing touches to the framework agreement on Pax Silica, expected to be signed by end of 2026, according to a trade senior official. – Rappler.com

Senate Social Media Unit

items: Lawyer Anel Martin Antero testified that Vice President Sara Duterte's lawyer, Mans Carpio, incurred a nearly P200,000 credit card bill for a group meal in Japan, which the defense team presented to explain his purchases.
During cross-examination, the prosecution questioned Antero's credibility, highlighting his close ties to the Duterte family and presenting social media posts that showed his pro-Duterte stance.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
To explain lawyer Mans Carpio’s big purchases, the defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte brought in lawyer Anel Martin Antero to the witness stand on Thursday, November 12.
During his testimony, Antero attributed Carpio’s nearly P200,000 credit card bill in May 2023 to a group meal in Japan.

But instead of dwelling on the explanation, the prosecution used its allotted time for cross-examination to cast doubt on Antero’s credibility. Specifically, the prosecution doubled down on the lawyer’s close ties to the Dutertes.
Prosecutor Amando Virgil Ligutan displayed several of Antero’s social media posts that revealed his pro-Duterte leanings on different issues.
At one point, Ligutan also showed a post where Antero referred to Duterte’s 2026 impeachment complaint as “flimsy.”
After minutes of being in the hot seat, Antero finally admitted his close ties to Duterte and her husband Mans.

“Now, do you also confirm that you have a close relationship with Attorney Carpio? Close relationship this time, not merely acquaintance, close relationship, these are two different things,” said Ligutan. “Yes,” said Antero.
“And you treat Attorney Manases Carpio like a brother, correct?” the prosecutor continued. “Yes, sir,” the lawyer responded.

blocks.caption: Like a brother? Duterte’s defense witness has close ties to Mans Carpio

blocks.text: Ligutan traced the money trail linking Carpio and Antero to show the extent of their relationship.
“Mr. Witness, did you ever receive money from Attorney Manases Garpio?” Ligutan asked.
“I am part of his firm, sir. From time to time, I receive some compensation from my professional services, sir,” said Antero.

The inquiry into large credit card purchases is meant to show that the Duterte family lives lavishly, despite claiming a modest lifestyle. This forms only a small part of the remaining article of impeachment.

The prosecution team relied on lawyer Alex Cabrera, an expert witness, to analyze Duterte’s financial records. He estimated that the Vice President had alleged P817 million in undeclared wealth from 2022 to 2025.
Among the transactions in the report are ¥489,000 spent at a restaurant in Ginza, Tokyo, and P256,000 at the Nike Pavilion in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.
Antero clarified that the Tokyo purchase was indeed for a meal, and it just so happened that they used Carpio’s card. He said he later paid Carpio for his part of the bill.

articles.title: Israel strikes Gaza hospital, says Hamas senior figure inside
articles.summary: Israel says Hamas was using the hospital as a military command center, while Palestinian officials report at least six people killed, including a surgeon. The strike comes amid an increasingly…

image.caption: Gaza authorities say many people were injured and six killed in the strikeImage: Ramadan Abed/REUTERS

blocks.text: Israel said it had targeted a senior Hamas member in a Gaza hospital in an overnight airstrike which reportedly killed six people.
According to the Israeli military, Muhammad Abu Ismail and other militants from the Islamist group had been operating a command center inside the Nasser hospital in Khan Yunis.
Gaza's civil defense service said at least six people were killed, including a surgeon and more than 20 were wounded. It said that parts of several floors were severely damaged or destroyed.
During war, hospitals are protected under international humanitarian law, although they can lose that protection if they are used for military purposes.
Israel says hospital used for terrorist activities

In a statement on Thursday, the Israeli military (IDF) said, without providing evidence, that Hamas was "operating within Nasser Hospital in Khan Yunis" and were using the complex "as a hub for military and terrorist activities against IDF troops and Israel."

The IDF identified the targeted senior Hamas member as Abu Ismail, adding he "was responsible for directing terrorist attacks against Israeli civilians & IDF troops and for holding numerous hostages captive throughout the war."
The IDF said the hospital was used for storing weapons, to conduct interrogation, operate command-and-control rooms as well as to shelter terrorists.
What happened at the hospital?
The Gaza Health Ministry said the Israeli airstrike hit the surgery department, killing six people including surgeon Rizk Abu Sharia.

blocks.caption: Mourners carry the body of surgeon Rizk Abu Sharia, who was killed in the Israeli strike at Nasser HospitalImage: Ramadan Abed/REUTERS

blocks.text: News agency Reuters reported seeing footage from inside the hospital showing extensive damage with debris scattered around rooms and equipment.
Wounded people were also seen in the wreckage while several bodies were being carried away as firefighters worked to clear the scene.
Hamas has described the strike as a "fully-fledged war crime."
Since the beginning of the war in 2023, Israeli forces have attacked several hospitals in the Gaza Strip.
Fragile ceasefire
The war on Hamas in Gaza began in October 2023 after Hamas-led militants attacked southern Israel, killing around 1,200 people and taking 251 hostages.
Since then, more than 74,000 people have been killed in Gaza, according to the Gaza Health Ministry, whose figures are generally considered reliable by the international community.
More than 1.6 million residents of Gaza's 2.1-million population now live in tents or other makeshift shelters due to Israel's war in the enclave.

A ceasefire came into effect in October 2025, but attacks have continued since then. While Israel says Hamas is trying to regroup, the Palestinian militant group says it's committed to the ceasefire and that Israel is trying to undermine the agreement.
Hamas is recognized as a terrorist organization by the EU, the US and several Arab states.

articles.title: Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in Gaza kills surgeon and five others
articles.summary:
Patients awaiting surgery die in attack on one of few remaining medical facilities in the strip, doctor says

An Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in southern Gaza killed six people,…
articles.byline: Seham Tantesh in Gaza and William Christou in Beirut

blocks.text: An Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in southern Gaza killed six people, including a surgeon and a disabled man, and wounded more than 20 others, the Palestinian news agency reported.

The Israeli military carried out the attack on the hospital, in Khan Younis, early on Thursday saying in a statement it had struck a Hamas commander and other fighters there, without providing evidence.

The strike destroyed part of the surgery department, and caused extensive damage to several floors. Videos showed smoke filling rubble-strewn hallways, with medical equipment broken and knocked over from the blast.

“The bombing caused thick smoke to fill the rooms and fires to break out, amid the groans of wounded and people’s screams. There were many casualties and blood everywhere … Most of us sustained injuries to our limbs, as well as shrapnel wounds in different parts of our bodies,” said Dr Ayman Abu Ubaid, a surgical specialist at Nasser medical complex who was wounded in the attack.

blocks.caption: Women mourn during the funeral of patients killed during the strike on Nasser hospital on Thursday. Photograph: Abed Rahim Khatib/Anadolu/Getty Images

blocks.text: Ubaid said the strike happened at about 12.30am, without warning. “The patients in the department were all surgical patients waiting to undergo operations. The bombing happened at a time when they should have been asleep,” he said.
Among the dead was Rizk Abu Shaira, a general surgeon who had been featured in a documentary about doctors operating in Gaza, called American Doctor.

“Dr Rizk was in the American Doctor documentary operating and serving his people. He lost his life doing that, he lost his life because he was doing that,” Dr Thaer Ahmad, who also featured in the documentary, posted on X.

Nasser hospital is one of the last functioning healthcare facilities in Gaza after Israeli bombing made most of the strip’s facilities unusable. Israel also struck the hospital last year, killing five journalists in a double-tap strike on a location often used by reporters for filming.

The Israeli military has accused Hamas of using hospitals as command centres and to store weapons, an accusation the militant movement rejects. More than 1,700 healthcare workers have been killed in Gaza, while Israel has detained hundreds of medics since 7 October 2023, with at least 95 still in custody, according to Doctors Without Borders (MSF).
About 90% of Gaza’s health infrastructure has been destroyed or damage by Israeli bombing, systematic destruction UN experts called “medicide”.
Attacking healthcare facilities and staff is illegal under international humanitarian law, though facilities can lose their protected status if they are used for military purposes.
There is an increased need for healthcare during the winter months in Gaza, where rains have displaced people from their tents and increased communicable diseases in crowded encampments.

One of those killed in Thursday’s strike was Seif Ghazi Abu Hatab, 29, who had checked in to Nasser hospital on Monday after a piece of debris fell on his back while he was helping clear rubble from a friend’s home. He was scheduled for surgery at 10am on Thursday, and was meant to receive further treatment abroad.

blocks.caption: A view of the destruction in Nasser hospital on Thursday. Photograph: Abed Rahim Khatib/Anadolu/Getty Images

blocks.text: “Seif was a young man in the prime of his life. He wanted to live, rebuild his home and start a normal life, free from problems and suffering … Seif was killed after already losing two of his brothers and his father. His mother has now lost three of her sons,” said his cousin Tareq Abu Hatab, 37.

Israel launched the war in Gaza after the 7 October 2023 Hamas-led attack that killed about 1,200 people and took 251 hostage. At least 74,645 people have since been killed in Gaza and Israel has carried out a genocide in the strip, according to the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory.
Israel continues to carry out airstrikes in Gaza, killing more than 1,600 people since the October 2025 “ceasefire” according to the Gaza ministry of health.

articles.title: Ombudsman suspends mayor of Rosario, Cavite, for alleged casino gambling
articles.summary: The 6-month preventive suspension without pay is a measure to guarantee an unbiased and unhindered administrative investigation, says the Ombudsman

blocks.text: ALLEGED GAMBLING. Rosario, Cavite Mayor Jose Voltaire Ricafrente allegedly left a casino in Bacolod City with four companions and P10,000 worth of winnings.
Photo from Rosario LGU
The 6-month preventive suspension without pay is a measure to guarantee an unbiased and unhindered administrative investigation, says the Ombudsman

The Office of the Ombudsman ordered on Thursday, November 12, the six-month preventive suspension of Mayor Jose Voltaire Ricafrente of Rosario, Cavite, over his alleged engagement in gambling activities at a casino in Bacolod City.

The order stemmed from a complaint filed by the Field Investigation Office (FIO) of the Office of the Ombudsman, which found that Ricafrente, along with four companions, entered the casino at a hotel on March 14, 2026.
The Rosario mayor allegedly played at a gaming table with P30,000 worth of casino chips and won P10,000 before leaving the casino.
Under Presidential Decree No. 1869 or the PAGCOR Charter and Memorandum Circular No. 6 s. 2016, government personnel are strictly prohibited from entering, staying, or playing in casinos.

“This Office finds sufficient grounds for the issuance of an Order for Preventive Suspension against respondent Municipal Mayor Jose Voltaire Ricafrente, Municipality of Rosario, Province of Cavite, considering that there is strong evidence showing his guilt; the charges against him for Grave Misconduct and Conduct Prejudicial to the Best Interest of the Service may warrant his removal from the service,” the six-page order stated.
Ricafrente will be preventively suspended without pay pending the resolution of the administrative charges against him.
The Ombudsman said a preventive suspension is not a penalty but serves as a measure to guarantee an unbiased and unhindered administrative investigation.

Ricafrente is a close ally of the Revilla dysnasty in Cavite. His municipality is within the Cavite 1st District represented by Jolo Revilla. Jose Voltaire is the son of the late former mayor Jose “Nonong” Ricafrente Jr., who served as provincial administrator when Bong Revilla Jr. was governor.
Rappler has reached out to the municipal government and Ricafrente’s office for a statement on the issue. This article will be updated with his reply. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Who could replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia's chief executive?
articles.summary: As uncertainty swirls over the boss of the AI chip giant, some names have emerged as potential successors.

blocks.text: Image source, Reuters
ByOsmond Chia
Business reporter
Nvidia is facing a scenario few would have considered until very recently - a future without Jensen Huang.

The chief executive and co-founder of the AI chip-making giant is at the centre of a major scandal over reports of extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.
Nvidia's board is reportedly meeting to discuss whether to replace Huang.
But finding the right person to lead the business that Huang helped create more than three decades ago and turned into the world's second most valuable company - after Apple - is a challenge.
We take a look at which candidates have emerged as potential successors.
The finance chief

blocks.caption: Image caption, Colette Kress is chief financial officer at Nvidia

blocks.text: Image source, Nvidia
Colette Kress is chief financial officer at Nvidia
Colette Kress, Nvidia's chief financial officer, has been tipped as someone who could steady the ship in the interim, and possibly stop its share price from plunging even further.
An industry veteran for more than 30 years, Kress previously held high positions at tech firms like Cisco and Microsoft.
Kress, who also serves as Nvidia's executive vice president, has seen the firm's transformation from making chips for video games in the early 1990s to becoming an AI semiconductor powerhouse.
She "fronts every earnings call" alongside Huang and is a "familiar and trusted voice for the market at a time when it badly needs one," said Josh Gilbert, an analyst at investment firm eToro.
But doing the job permanently could be a different story, said Gilbert, as the firm, known for its edge in technology, could want an engineer in the chair.
The co-founder and the engineer

blocks.caption: Image caption, Chris Malachowsky is one of Nvidia's three co-founders

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
Chris Malachowsky is one of Nvidia's three co-founders
Another option is Chris Malachowsky, who founded Nvidia alongside Huang and Curtis Priem, and is the only executive that shares the same level of seniority.
Malachowsky has played a key part in developing the company's computing technology.
Ian Buck, who oversees Nvidia's high-performance computing business, has also emerged as a potential candidate if the company is keen to put an engineer in the top job.
Buck was among the early pioneers who helped popularise the use of graphic processors beyond gaming applications.

"He could protect Nvidia's technological edge, but his ability to manage the wider commercial relationships and geopolitical challenges would face scrutiny," said Charu Chanana, investment strategist at investment bank Saxo.
Today, Nvidia's leading processors are widely regarded as the gold standard for AI development.
Huang's children also work at Nvidia in executive positions but are relatively young and inexperienced.
Apple and Arm's top brass
Nvidia is likely to favour an internal appointment initially but could look externally for a more permanent replacement, said Jun Bei Liu, founder and lead portfolio manager at Ten Cap.
Several names of tech entrepreneurs outside of Nvidia have been floated by experts.

Liu said Apple's former chief executive, Tim Cook, could be a possible choice as someone familiar with managing global supply chains, though she questioned whether he would be willing to leave the iPhone maker, where he is the chair.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Apple's Tim Cook (R) with Jensen Huang (L) and his wife Lori Huang at the White House

blocks.text: Apple's Tim Cook (R) with Jensen Huang (L) and his wife Lori Huang at the White House
Liu and Chanana also suggested Rene Haas, chief executive of Arm Holdings, the UK chipmaking giant.
Nvidia's processors are made with the help of chipmakers around the world, including Taiwan's TSMC and South Korea's SK Hynix and Samsung.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Rene Haas is the boss of Arm Holdings

blocks.text: Rene Haas is the boss of Arm Holdings
Haas is familiar with leading a publicly-listed company and would bring semiconductor experience, though Nvidia's business model is considerably different from Arm's, said Chanana.
"The challenge is finding someone who can combine Jensen's technical understanding, strategic vision and relationships across the global technology industry," Liu said.
Where now for Huang?
Ten Cap's Liu believes it is a matter of time in terms of Huang stepping down as Nvidia's chief executive.

"The issue is no longer simply about personal conduct," she said. "It is about corporate governance, national security concerns and maintaining confidence in the leadership of one of the world's most strategically important companies."
Several major investment firms have downgraded their forecasts for the chip giant - a rare shift given investors' longstanding optimism about the company.
Stacy Rasgon, senior analyst in US semiconductors at Bernstein Research, wrote in a note to investors that "our gut tells us we probably haven't fully probed the depths of what might be found here".
Rasgon halved Bernstein's share price target for Nvidia and said: "We've had enough and prefer to watch from the sidelines."

Ray Wang, chief executive of Constellation Research, said the crisis isn't so much an issue for the wider AI industry but rather one for Nvidia itself which has to consider if the person it appoints as its chief executive has the same appeal as Huang.
"That's really what the issue is, because a lot of these partnerships and investments have been made because of the trust with with Jensen," he said.
Additional reporting by Kali Hays

articles.title: Yella Beezy found guilty in murder-for-hire of fellow Dallas rapper
articles.summary: Rapper Yella Beezy was found guilty on Wednesday of hiring the gunman who fatally shot rapper MO3 in a brazen daylight attack on a busy Dallas interstate in 2020.

image.caption: Musician Yella Beezy, whose real name is Markies Conway, sits in court during his murder-for-hire trial in Dallas on Tuesday. Jurors found him guilty after deliberating for six hours. (LM Otero/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New
Rapper Yella Beezy was found guilty on Wednesday of hiring the gunman who fatally shot rapper MO3 in a brazen daylight attack on a busy Dallas interstate in 2020.
Gunman Kewon White was found guilty in September for fatal shooting of Melvin Noble, known as MO3

Yella Beezy, 35, whose real name is Markies Conway, was unanimously convicted of capital murder by a Dallas County jury in the death of MO3, whose real name was Melvin Noble. He was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole.
In September, a jury found Kewon White guilty of capital murder for fatally shooting Noble. He was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole.
Prosecutors said the killing was the result of an yearslong escalating feud between Conway and Noble. Both men lived in Dallas.
"We don't know what turned it for the jurors.… We appreciate the verdict," lead prosecutor Tommy Adams told reporters. "We think they got it right today.
"It's been one of the most challenging cases over the last six years," he added.
Conway is best known for his 2017 single That's On Me, and the 2019 song Bacc At It Again with Quavo and Gucci Mane.
Noble had more than 800,000 Instagram followers and is best known for a 2019 remix of Errybody with Baton Rouge, La., rapper Boosie Badazz.
Revenge theory floated after earlier shooting
Noble, 28, was driving on Interstate 35 in south Dallas around noon on Nov. 11, 2020, when White pulled alongside him, authorities said. White stepped out of his vehicle holding a gun.
Noble got out of his own vehicle and began running on the freeway as White shot at him, authorities said.
MO3 is shown at a BET Awards event in Los Angeles on June 23, 2018, just over two years before he was shot. (Alberto E. Rodriguez/Getty Images for BET)
Adams said White wore a mask and fired over 40 rounds from an AK-47-style pistol while chasing Noble.
White shot Noble and a bystander who was inside a car, police said. The bystander survived, but Noble died at a hospital.
Prosecutors said Conway paid White $40,000 US for the shooting.

blocks.text: During closing arguments, prosecutors showed jurors a video clip of Conway talking about revenge in an interview, saying he would "get his lick back." Prosecutor Krystal Biggins drew a comparison between Noble's killing and a roadway shooting that injured Conway in 2018.
In October 2018, Conway survived being shot while driving on a tollway in the Dallas suburb of Lewisville when someone pulled up next to him and opened fire, hitting him three times.
"This was for the world to see," Biggins said. "Over a rap beef, we are here for capital murder."
The defence argued that prosecutors did not prove their case. "This is capital murder, and the state has brought you a lot of speculation," defence lawyer John Gussio said.

articles.title: European survey reveals 900m galaxies – and possibly secrets of ‘dark universe’
articles.summary:
Unprecedented view of cosmos provided by Euclid mission throws up many more cases of gravitational lensing

A mission to create the largest ever 3D map of the universe has revealed more than…

blocks.text: A mission to create the largest ever 3D map of the universe has revealed more than 900m galaxies in its first major data release together with about 15,000 potential cases of a phenomenon that could help unlock the secrets of the “dark universe”.
Launched in July 2023, the European Space Agency’s Euclid mission promised to create the largest cosmic map ever made, encompassing a third of the sky and more than 10bn years of cosmic history.
The goal is to shed light on two of the biggest mysteries in the universe: the nature of dark energy and dark matter. These are thought to make up about 70% and 25% of the universe respectively.

Prof Andy Taylor, of the University of Edinburgh, who leads the UK science ground segment for the mission, said while there were bigger surveys, none had the detail and the information content of Euclid. By contrast the Hubble telescope has produced images of incredible resolution, but does not cover as large an area of the sky.
“The technological leap that’s Euclid is that we can keep that high resolution, but now we can basically map huge volumes of the sky, huge volumes of the universe,” Taylor said.

blocks.caption: The Euclid mission is intended to create the largest ever 3D map of the universe.  Photograph: Esa/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/Nasa; Esa/Gaia/DPAC; Esa/Planck Collaboration, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO

blocks.text: Now, the first major Euclid data release has landed, offering researchers an unprecedented view of the cosmos. “It’s the biggest high-resolution image of the universe we’ve ever had,” Taylor said.

Covering about 14% of the total area of sky that will be mapped by Euclid, the newly released data captures over 900m galaxies as well more than 60m potential quasars: blazing objects at the centre of distant galaxies, powered by supermassive black holes.

It also includes a tranche of candidates for what was previously considered a rare phenomenon: strong gravitational lensing. This is a magnification effect that occurs when one galaxy, often embedded in a galaxy cluster, sits in front of another, distant galaxy.

As Taylor notes, Einstein predicted the gravitational influence of the foreground galaxy would distort space-time, bending the light from the background galaxy and creating the appearance of bright arcs or rings. Crucially, the effect is significantly boosted by the presence of dark matter, which increases the mass and hence gravitational influence of a galaxy.

Taylor said that by studying strong gravitational lensing, scientists may be able to rule out different theories on the nature of dark matter. That is because the lensing is influenced by how this mysterious substance is distributed in a galaxy – that itself depends on its properties.

blocks.caption: Abell 3128, a cluster of hundreds of galaxies lying about 800m light-years away from Earth, is seen in this image captured by the European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope. Photograph: Esa/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/Nasa/Reuters

blocks.text: Stephen Serjeant, a professor of astronomy at the Open University, agreed. “With strong gravitational lensing, you find out how the dark matter is clumping and that’s very diagnostic of the type of matter that it is, because different types of matter can clump in very different ways,” he said.

“So if you’re looking for where the next breakthrough will be in the properties of dark matter and what dark matter actually is, there’s a good chance – I can’t say it’s certain – but there’s a good chance it might come from strong gravitational lensing.”

Taylor noted that while experts previously knew of about 1,000 cases of strong gravitational lensing, the Euclid data contains about 15,000 probable cases, with an estimated 170,000 expected to be discovered by the end of the mission.

A further release of data was expected to land next summer, Taylor added, which will include results on both the distribution of galaxies as well as weak gravitational lensing – subtle distortions in distant objects by dark matter in the foreground.

“We can use that pattern of distortions to actually make a map of where all the dark matter is in the universe,” said Taylor, adding that scientists could then work out its statistical properties and compare the results with different theories. “Depending on the type of dark matter, the type of dark energy, we’re expecting to see slightly different patterns on the sky.”
And with Euclid generating ever-more data, Taylor noted there was plenty to explore.

“It’s opening up that high resolution of the whole sky, the whole universe. So it just means there are plenty of objects that we’ll never have seen before, plenty of research phenomena,” he said. “No human eyeball is able to look at all of the Euclid data any more. It’s now too big.”

articles.title: Art exhibit raises funds for Banaue’s Good News Clinic and Hospital
articles.summary: PRESS RELEASE: The exhibit runs from November 14 to December 6, 2026, at the GCF Ortigas Fellowship Hall in Pasig City. Proceeds will be dedicated to the expansion of the hospital in Ifugao.

blocks.text: This is a press release from the Good News Clinic and Hospital in Banaue, Ifugao.

As part of its 70th anniversary celebration, Good News Clinic and Hospital (GNCH), a non-profit mission hospital that has served in Banaue, Ifugao, is set to hold its fourth “Art for GoodNews’ Sake” fundraiser.
With the theme “Instrumento Tayo!” the exhibit will be happening from November 14 to December 6, 2026, at the GCF Ortigas Fellowship Hall in Pasig City.
It will feature pieces donated by over 70 Filipino artists and creatives, including Ed Uygongco, Rey Aurelio, Addie Cukingnan, Chino Yulo, Vincent Louie Tan, and Coeli Manese.

The annual art show seeks to raise over P5 million for GNCH’s Ipaphod Transformation Project, which includes the establishment of a new emergency room, triage extension, patient lift, and a ramp for the hospital.

GNCH was founded in 1956 by USAFFE medical corps veteran missionary Dr. James Irvine in Barrio Tam-an in Banaue. It endured throughout the years under the leadership of other missionary doctors, including Dr. Antonio Ligot, who served the clinic and hospital for over three decades.

Currently, the Philhealth Yakap-accredited hospital is led by Dr. Carolyn Abayao, a Banaue native once treated at GNCH following a tragic accident at age 13. She had served there as a nurse under Dr. Ligot’s tutelage prior to pursuing her general medicine degree.

“It is only by the grace of God, and His providential work through the selfless hands of missionary doctors and generous donors that GNCH still stands to serve the people of Banaue for 70 years and stay true to its mission of ‘Healing Bodies and Winning Souls to Christ,’” GNCH administrator Dan Andrew Cura said.
“We are truly grateful for the artists who contributed their works for our annual art show and call for the public’s continued support for the hospital.” – Rappler.com

GCF Ortigas, which hosts the annual art show, is located at the corner of Garnet and Ruby roads, Ortigas Center, Pasig City. Persons interested to contribute to GNCH’s medical work can reach out to the following official channels: GNCH website, Facebook, email, and mobile +63968 1441 956.

Even as Yin Yeung Derek Chan went to prison earlier this year, the actions of Canada's most prolific voyeur continued to "irrevocably scar" the lives of victims, a judge said. Chan had uploaded many of the "countless" videos and images secretly recorded of at least 652 women and children online.
Images produced by Yin Yeung Derek Chan will continue to 'irrevocably scar' victims, judge says

When Yin Yeung Derek Chan went to prison earlier this year, a judge said the photographs and videos Chan produced as Canada's most prolific voyeur would continue to "irrevocably scar" the lives of victims.

The judge said Chan recorded "countless" videos and images of at least 652 women and girls in Greater Victoria without their consent and uploaded many online — where some have continued to spread even after the voyeur's sentencing.
After an investigation by CBC News, a team of researchers at one Canadian charity has spent months working to take down as many of these images as they can, including several posted to social media.

"I deal with this stuff every day, but [this case] was really unique in terms of the volume [of images]," said Lloyd Richardson, director of technology for the Canadian Centre for Child Protection (CCCP).
"It was just absolutely sickening."

items: 'Hunted,' 'shattered,' 'scared': How victims say Canada's most prolific voyeur has altered their lives

blocks.text: Court records show Saanich police apprehended Chan in 2024 after some of the images the voyeur uploaded online were flagged by the National Centre for Missing and Exploited Children.

In a search warrant application, Saanich police wrote that officers confronted Chan with allegations that the voyeur had recorded hundreds of victims, and uploaded more than 100 of these files online.
"Something like that, I've lost count," Chan said, according to the records.
Victims in Canada's largest voyeurism case felt 'hunted'

One Reddit post created by Chan — tagged "NSFW", meaning not safe for work — contained 19 images which appeared to be taken of girls and young women, without their knowledge, while they were shopping.
Commenters asked where to find videos Chan filmed, to which the voyeur responds they're "only open to payers."
"I am ready to follow and pay if necessary," writes one commenter. "Thank you for your work."
Canada's largest voyeurism case has 652 victims
Reddit did not respond to multiple messages from CBC News about the post — but removed it and banned Chan's account within hours of receiving concerns from the CCCP.
Richardson says Reddit's own moderation system failed to catch what he believes is a violation of its terms of service.
The site's process for reporting, he said, also made efforts by outside groups to report child sexual abuse material or non-consensual intimate images more challenging.

items: Girls in school uniforms among hundreds filmed by Saanich voyeur, court records reveal

blocks.text: Other companies have sent responses to the CCCP's takedown requests, declining to comply, that Richardson said he believes are generated by artificial intelligence — which he said can be time-consuming to escalate.
"There's a little bit of a David and Goliath thing going on there, with a multi-billion tech company versus a small charity in Canada," he said.
"The art of removal is a complicated thing, and dealing with the big tech companies is just sort of one avenue of it."
The Canadian Centre for Child Protection is located in Winnipeg. (Canadian Centre for Child Protection)
One of the tools the CCCP uses to remove and prevent the reuploading of child sexual abuse material online is Project Arachnid, an automated image detection program.

While the CCCP has been successful in tracking down some images of Chan's victims, Richardson said it has been challenging, given the large number of victims and limited public information to use in their search.

Often, the CCCP begins their work after the police or a victim reaches out with specific information about where images are online — which Richardson said is easier for the charity to fully shut down.
But in this case, the CCCP was alerted through the CBC investigation, which has left them to rely on information available through court records.
He hopes victims will also reach out, if they are concerned their images may be online.
'Devastated' lives, judge says
When delivering Chan's sentence earlier this year, B.C. Provincial Court Judge Lisa Mrozinski said the online recordings would continue to cause harm for years to come.
While several websites that Chan posted to — including one with over a million views — have been removed, some of the recordings have been shared by other online users, the court heard.
"Know that you have devastated and possibly irrevocably scarred the lives of countless women," Mrozinski said to the voyeur.

"These are women who must now live with the knowledge that these images live on the internet. There are the many others who will find out soon, and the many, many others who may never know, yet will be victimized, every time such images are viewed online."

items: Police did not intervene as Canada's most prolific voyeur was 'looking for more victims,' court records show

blocks.text: As Richardson's team continues to look for more recordings created by Chan, they're also pushing for policy changes to protect potential future victims.

He's hopeful for the federal government's proposed Safe Social Media Act, which would create a regulatory body to hold companies accountable, and the barriers it may remove for taking down child sexual abuse material.
"They're basically going to be an instrument of bringing the hammer down on some of these companies, and that's great," he said.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Emily Fagan is a CBC News journalist based in Victoria, B.C. She was previously a staff reporter for the Toronto Star. Her work has also appeared in publications including the Globe and Mail, Vice and the Washington Post. You can reach her at emily.fagan@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Zubiri urges: Move on, tackle other issues on Sara Duterte's 'unexplained wealth'
articles.summary: Senator-judge Juan Miguel Zubiri on Thursday urged that the discussion in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte "move on" to other key issues regarding her alleged unexplained wealth,…

blocks.text: Published November 12, 2026 6:59pm

Senator-judge Juan Miguel Zubiri on Thursday urged that the discussion in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte "move on" to other key issues regarding her alleged unexplained wealth, including the supposed inflow of money from China through a company linked to her husband, Manases Carpio.
Zubiri made the call after the defense presented two witness, lawyer Anel Antero and Chad Parian, who testified on Carpio's credit card purchases worth over P200,000 each.

Antero testified that he partly reimbursed Carpio for the P200,000-meal they ate at Ginza in Tokyo, Japan, while Parian testified that Carpio paid for over P256,000 worth of shoes for the young players of the Elite Basketball team and their parents in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.
Parian said his son and that of Carpio played for the same team in a tournament in Malaysia where the team won the championship.
Zubiri expressed readiness to tackle about other matters concerning the vice president.

"I think we are belaboring the point. He (Carpio) did spend money for the team. You (The prosecution) made your point that it could be ostentatious. Of course, the defense is saying that they were reimbursed. Ok na siguro 'yan (I think that's enough)," Zubiri said.

Prosecution witnesses included Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura, who confirmed that the Carpio-linked Cale88 Foods Corporation received P319 million from China and Hong Kong.

Financial forensic analyst Alexander Cabrera, another witness for the prosecution, testified that the undeclared assets and unexplained wealth of Duterte and Carpio amounted to at least P817.87 million, to as high as about P1.5 billion, from 2022 to 2025.

"What I am more interested in is not on the spending of this credit card. I am more interested saan napunta iyong 300 million foreign deposits sa Cale88 [Foods Corporation]. Saan galing 'yun? Anong ginawa sa pera? May mga documentation ba na nabayaran ang kanilang dividend stocks?…Things like that. Let's move on and maybe let's listen to other witnesses and give us the more substantive answers to the cases at hand," Zubiri added.

(What I am more interested in is not on the spending of this credit card. I am more interested on where the 300 million foreign deposits for Cale88 ended up. Where is this payout coming from? What was done with the money? Are these documented in terms of paid dividend stocks?)
Cale88 is a declared asset of the Vice President's husband, Attorney Carpio, in multiple years.

Defense counsel Sheila Sison informed the Senate impeachment court that she and her colleagues do not intend to present Quezon City prosecutor Vimar Barcellano as witness as scheduled, provided that the prosecution will stipulate on agreeing that Barcellano is a competent witness to authenticate documentary evidence presented by the defense.
The prosecution stipulated on this matter, prompting the early adjournment of the trial around 12:30 p.m. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Sara Duterte defense team eyes 8 to 10 more witnesses in impeachment trial
articles.summary: The defense team is planning to present at least eight more witnesses to testify in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, counsel Michael Poa said Thursday.

blocks.text: Published November 12, 2026 6:53pm
The defense team is planning to present at least eight more witnesses to testify in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, counsel Michael Poa said Thursday.

In a press briefing, Poa said that the defense is trying to “speed things up” with regard to the presentation of evidence for Article II of the impeachment case, alleging Duterte’s unexplained wealth.

“Sa atin naman (for us), as long as we are able to make the points we want to make, to provide the Vice President with the best defense we can provide her, then we should be okay with that,” the defense lawyer said in a post-trial press conference.
Poa noted that the defense has two full trial days next week, after the break for the conduct of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits, to present its remaining witnesses.

He said the defense would assess if they could finish its presentation of evidence by the end of next week so as to not lose the momentum when the trial goes on break anew to pave the way for the 2027 national budget deliberations.

“Kung maputol ‘yung testimony ng witness, meron tayong break for the budget plenary, mawawala ‘yung momentum plus baka hindi ma-fully appreciate hindi lang ng senator-judges, but pati ng publiko ‘yung sinusubukan nating gawin,” Poa explained.

(If the witnesses’ testimony gets cut, we’ll lose momentum, considering the upcoming break for the plenary budget deliberations. The public and the senator-judges might not also get to fully appreciate what we’re trying to do when that happens.)

“In fact, I would rather na…ma-cut short, meaning matapos kami nang mas maaga next week kaysa ‘yung mabitin siya in the end. So we're just trying to assess how to present witnesses na hindi makakasayang ng oras ng court, but at the same time hindi rin mapuputol for the long break,” he added.

(In fact, I would rather have our presentation of evidence be cut short, meaning we conclude earlier than expected, rather than leave it hanging. So, we are currently assessing how to present witnesses in a way that avoids wasting the court’s time, while also ensuring that their testimonies do not get affected by the long break.)

Impeachment court spokesperson Regie Tongol, meanwhile, said they expect that the remaining witnesses of the defense include a forensic expert, just like that of the prosecution at the end of the presentation of its own evidence.

“The impeachment court is assuming some or one or two of the witnesses that they said they will present out of the eight will be either ‘yung forensic analyst na ‘yun,” Tongol said in a separate press briefing. —NB, GMA News

articles.title: Young people should get fewer welfare benefits, according to Milburn review on the workforce – UK politics live
articles.summary:
Milburn’s review is considering how to address the growing number of young people classified as not in education, employment or training

“Britain is back and ready to play its full part,”…

blocks.text: Key events

items: 2m agoEU Parliament president pledges support for UK-EU reset ahead of next week's summit
15m ago'The world will breach the 1.5c target,' Burnham tells Cop31 summit
25m agoUnder-25s could be moved off key sickness and disability benefits in welfare shake-up

blocks.text: EU Parliament president pledges support for UK-EU reset ahead of next week's summit

blocks.caption: Jakub Krupa

blocks.text: Jakub Krupa

Over in Dublin, where the European Political Community summit is taking place, European parliament president Roberta Metsola told journalists she would do “anything in my power” to turn the political intent behind the announced UK-EU reset plan into “very tangible steps”.

blocks.caption: President of the European parliament, Roberta Metsola, speaks to the media ahead of the European Political Community summit in Dublin.  Photograph: Liam McBurney/PA

blocks.text: “We have a very solid UK-EU parliamentary assembly and partnership, and that is the partnership that we will be using in order to make sure that any agreement and all measures that are taken next week during the [EU-UK] summit will be implemented through majorities in parliament,” she said.
“That is what I hope for, and I am extremely optimistic in that regard,” she added, describing herself as “a big fan of the United Kingdom”.
For more updates from across Europe, follow our live blog here:
'The world will breach the 1.5c target,' Burnham tells Cop31 summit

blocks.caption: Ajit Niranjan

blocks.text: Ajit Niranjan
“Britain is back and ready to play its full part,” Andy Burnham has said at the opening of today’s Cop31 summit.

The UK prime minister celebrated domestic clean energy projects including windfarms and electrified steel factories, stressed the need to make the transition affordable, and announced the UK’s first special representative for climate security, Madeleine Alessandri.

“The climate crisis is not a distant threat, it is upon us now, devastating lives and livelihoods everywhere,” he said. Pointing to the effects of two global wars on energy prices, he added that the “common thread running through all of this is fossil fuels.”
Burnham repeated the UK’s commitment to meeting its 2050 net zero emissions target and said he would work with all of partners to reach theirs.

blocks.caption: Andy Burnham addresses the Cop31 annual UN climate conference in Antalya, Turkey. Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPA

blocks.text: “In that spirit, I am proud to support this Cop’s focus on electrification,” he said. “If we depend on energy we do not control, we depend on prices we cannot control. The shift to clean energy is the only route to energy security.
He called on industry to “play their part” in helping people on all incomes make the green transition. He highlighted progress in bringing the price of clean technologies down for consumers.
“If you drive a new electric car today in the UK, it costs less than a petrol equivalent. Get on the right tariff and a heat pump can be cheaper to run than a gas boiler.”
But he also warned that some of the fundamentals had worsened.
“The consensus we once enjoyed on science is gone,” said Burnham. “And the reality is the world will breach the 1.5C target.”
For more updates from the fourth day of the climate summit in Turkey, head over to our Cop31 live blog here:
Under-25s could be moved off key sickness and disability benefits in welfare shake-up

Good morning and welcome to the UK politics live blog. Young people could lose entitlement to the main sickness and disability benefits under a significant overhaul of the welfare system, according to proposals expected to emerge from the government-commissioned review into young people and work.

Led by former health secretary Alan Milburn, the review is examining the barriers preventing young people from entering the workforce and how to address the growing number classified as not in education, employment or training (Neet), which currently stands at about 981,000 across the UK.

blocks.caption: Alan Milburn (right) speaking to apprentices at the Irish Rail training centre in Inchicore, Dublin, in August. Photograph: Patrick Bolger/The Guardian

blocks.text: The review, which has been under way for a year, is expected to include proposals that would remove under-25s’ entitlement to the health element of universal credit and personal independence payment (Pip), replacing them with a standard-rate youth allowance. Under the plans, first reported by the Times, those with additional needs arising from a disability would receive a separate, non-means-tested allowance, while those with severe disabilities and who are not capable of working would qualify for a higher rate.

Speaking to the newspaper, Milburn acknowledged that the changes would not be “pain-free”, admitting some young people could initially receive less financial support than under the current system. The final review is due to be published on Tuesday.
In other news:

items: Prime minister Andy Burnham addressed world leaders at Cop31 in Turkey, pledging a “new era of British leadership” on climate change and reaffirming the UK’s commitment to its 2050 net-zero target. He said international consensus on science and climate “has gone”, adding: “The reality is the world will breach the 1.5C target.” You can keep up to date with the latest from the Cop31 summit in our live blog here:

articles.title: PCG, BFAR complete first high seas fisheries inspection mission
articles.summary: A team from the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) and the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) returned to Manila Thursday after completing their first High Seas Boarding and Inspection (HSBI)…

blocks.text: Published November 12, 2026 6:37pm

The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) and the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR), aboard BRP Teresa Magbanua, return to Manila on Thursday, Nov. 12, after completing their first High Seas Boarding and Inspection mission under the Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Commission. (Photo from Danny Pata)

A team from the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) and the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) returned to Manila Thursday after completing their first High Seas Boarding and Inspection (HSBI) mission.
Aboard the PCG's BRP Teresa Magbanua, the team went on the mission under the Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Commission (WCPFC) for around 30 days.
The HSBI operations allowed inspectors to board and inspect fishing vessels at sea to detect, document, deter and respond to fisheries violations.
This mission was conducted as part of the Philippines' commitment as a WCPFC member to the long-term conservation and sustainable use of highly migratory fish stocks, including tuna.

Under the joint arrangement, BFAR provides fisheries regulatory, inspection and enforcement expertise, while the PCG supplies the inspection vessel and maritime operational support, including navigation, safety, security and boarding capabilities.—Joviland Rita/LDF, GMA News
