articles.title: Mans Carpio's friend admits no proof of Japan dinner reimbursement
articles.summary: The friend of Vice President Sara Duterte’s husband said he has no proof that he partly reimbursed more than P200,000 of his credit card bill in Japan.

blocks.text: November 12, 2026 | 6:30pm
Lawyer Arnel Antero, the friend of Vice President Sara Duterte and Manases Carpio during the impeachment trial on Nov. 12, 2026.
Senate PRIB
MANILA, Philippines — The friend of Vice President Sara Duterte’s husband said he has no proof that he partly reimbursed more than P200,000 of his credit card bill in Japan.

During his testimony on Thursday, November 12, lawyer Anel Antero, the witness presented by the defense panel, said the purchase was made for 11 individuals when he and Manases Carpio were dining at a restaurant in Ginza, Japan.
According to Antero, he was with Carpio and nine other law school friends when they dined in Ginza and used Carpio’s credit card to pay the bill.
The bill reportedly amounted to P205,007.29.
He said he later reimbursed Carpio with 40,000 Japanese yen, or around P16,000.
Antero also recalled that all 11 individuals who dined with Carpio had cash but were short of funds.
Prosecution lawyer Virgil Ligutan then questioned Antero on why, among the 11 individuals who dined with Carpio, the Vice President’s husband was the only one who offered to pay the bill.
Antero then said: “I don’t see anything magical about that, sir.”
“Ang totoo po niyan marami pong nag-volunteer na credit card nila ang gamitin, pero si Attorney Mans…” Antero added.
(The truth is, many people actually volunteered to let their credit cards be used, but Attorney Mans…)
Ligutan then asked if Antero had proof that he partly reimbursed Carpio, to which Antero replied: “Wala po.” (There is none).
Prosecution forensic analyst Alexander Cabrera previously flagged the May 2023 Tokyo restaurant charge as an unusually large personal expenditure while examining the couple’s finances.

The prosecution connected it to allegations that Duterte amassed about P817.87 million in undeclared assets and income and failed to fully disclose her assets in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth.

Ligutan also raised that the relevant question was not merely whether Carpio could afford the meal, but whether a single dinner worth P205,000 was consistent with the constitutional expectation that public officials and their families lead modest lives.

“This is central to the unexplained wealth, Your Honor. This is in the law, public officials and members of their family should lead a modest life. How is that irrelevant? Being the spouse of the Vice President does not make him immune from the requirements of leading a modest life, Your Honor,” Ligutan said.
This issue is being tackled under Article II of the Articles of Impeachment against Duterte.
The said article tackles allegations of ill-gotten wealth and non-declaration of her SALNs.

articles.title: Palace says P22.9-B ASEAN Summit spending open to audit amid scrutiny
articles.summary: The government is prepared to audit its spending for the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit, Malacañang said amid questions raised online about the expenses.

blocks.text: Published November 12, 2026 6:28pm
The government is prepared to audit its spending for the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit, Malacañang said amid questions raised online about the expenses.

"Handa ang gobyerno na ito ay ma-audit. Handa ang gobyernong mag-report para ipakita sa inyo kung saan napunta lahat ang ating pinaghandaan bilang host ng ASEAN Summit," Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said in a press briefing on Thursday.
(The government is ready to be audited. The government is ready to report to show the public where all the preparations we made as hosts of the ASEAN Summit went.)
The government has allocated P22.9 billion for the ASEAN Summit, as it marks its fifth time to chair the regional bloc.
Castro said instead of looking at the spending on ASEAN, the public should look at the gains the country is getting and will get in the future.

Castro made the statement as posts circulated online comparing the government's ASEAN budget of the Marcos administration to the Arroyo and Duterte administrations, which had P1 billion and P3.79 billion, respectively.

"Mas dapat natin tignan ano yung nasakop, ano yung nagawa, ano yung maaari maging risulta nito kesa sa ano yung nagastos noon at kung ano yung magagastos ngayon. Dahil alam naman nating ang Pangulo; ang pondo ng bayan dapat nababalik sa bayan" Castro said.

(We should look more at what has been achieved, what has been accomplished, what the results can be rather than what has been spent in the past and what will be spent now. Because we know the President, the people's funds should be returned to the people.)
Among the preparations done for the Summit are infrastructure and venue preparations, and security and emergency resources.
Attract investors in ASEAN
Castro also refuted claims that the clearing operations and installation of barricades in Pasay City were aimed at improving President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s image.
She said the government is conducting clearing operations not only for security purposes but also to attract international investors during the Summit.
"To suffer? Because of the vanity of the President? Bakit ang Pangulo ba nagpapaganda sa sarili niya?Ano ba ang pinapaganda natin, hindi ba ang Pilipinas?" Castro questioned.
(To suffer? Because of the vanity of the President? Why is the President making himself look good? What he is beautfying in the Philippines.)

"Pinapaganda natin ang Pilipinas para makita ng ibang bansa na ang Pilipinas ay isang mapagkakatiwalaang bansa kung saan puwede silang maglagak ng investments. Anong gusto nilang makita sa ating bansa? Isang maduming bansa?" she added.

(We are making the Philippines beautiful so that other countries can see that the Philippines is a trustworthy country where they can invest. What do they want to see in our country? A dirty country.)
Castro's statement was in reaction to BAYAN's statement that "people are being made to suffer" because of the "vanity" of President Ferdinand Marcos. Jr.

"Wag nilang ipahid kay pangulo ang lahat ng mga pagbibintang nang walang anumang basehan. Hindi mismo ang pangulo ang nagpapaganda sa sarili niya. Ang pinapaganda niya ay bansa at ang kapakanan ng bawat Pilipino," Castro said.

(They should not point all these baseless accusations at the President. The President is not the one who is making himself look good, but the country and the welfare of every Filipino.) —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Palace hopeful South China Sea COC will be signed before ASEAN chairmanship ends
articles.summary: Malacañang on Thursday said it is still hopeful that the Code of Conduct (COC) in the South China Sea would be signed before the Philippines' Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)…

blocks.text: Published November 12, 2026 6:24pm

Malacañang on Thursday said it is still hopeful that the Code of Conduct (COC) in the South China Sea would be signed before the Philippines' Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) chairmanship ends.
"Bawat araw dapat may pag-asa (we should have hope every day)," Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said during a press briefing.

"Sa ngayon, hindi rin natin masasabi kung talagang hindi ito magkakaroon ng konkulsyon sa 49th ASEAN Summit dahil ang gusto pa rin ng Pangulo ay masa-pinal sa panahon na ang Pilipinas ang ASEAN chair," she added.
(As of now, we cannot say if the COC will be concluded during the 49th ASEAN Summit because President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. want to finalized it during the Philippines’ chairmanship.)

Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro earlier said ASEAN and China do not want the South China Sea to have a situation like that in the Strait of Hormuz, the reason they negotiate to com up with a code of conduct.

The conflict in the Middle East has disrupted the shipment of petroleum products through the Strait of Hormuz—considered the world’s most vital oil export route—causing significant supply concerns globally.
This has driven up fuel prices in the different parts of the world, including the Philippines.

On July 12, 2016, the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague ruled that China’s sweeping claims over nearly the entire South China Sea had no legal basis under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), but China has rejected the ruling.
Tensions have nevertheless persisted as China claims almost the entire South China Sea, a major waterway through which more than $3 trillion in annual shipborne commerce passes.
Parts of the sea are also claimed by the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei, and Indonesia. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: ‘Like priests who don’t believe in God’: Italy’s anti-vax medics eye return to frontline duty
articles.summary:
Progress of bill to reinstate struck-off doctors hinged on support from far right figure Roberto Vannacci, whose rise is shaping politics before 2027 elections

Antonio Cremasco contracted…

blocks.text: Antonio Cremasco contracted Covid at a dinner party on 6 March 2020. Four days later, as Italy became the first European country to go into nationwide lockdown, he was fighting for his life. “I spent 20 days in intensive care, followed by another 20 days in a hospital ward,” said Cremasco, from Bassano del Grappa in the northern Italian Veneto region.

After leaving hospital, he needed oxygen therapy for another six months. Cremasco’s ordeal was such that when Covid vaccines became available in Italy in early 2021, he had no qualms about being vaccinated, and he believes the decision saved his life once again.
“All those who had been in intensive care with me died,” he said. “Without the vaccine, if I had caught Covid again, I had a high risk of dying too.”

blocks.caption: Doctors treating Covid patients in an intensive care unit at a Rome hospital in March 2020. Photograph: Antonio Masiello/Getty Images

blocks.text: But Cremasco, who is now 76 and recently received his annual Covid and winter flu jab, has struggled to convince his vaccine-sceptic son, a father of two, of the drugs’ safety. He said he and his wife were wary of having their potentially unvaccinated grandchildren in their home whenever the children were ill, fearing for their own health. “They always seem to be sick,” Cremasco said.
His family rift mirrors a wider divide over vaccination in Italy, which has been brought back to the political spotlight by a controversial bill approved in October in the lower house of parliament.

The measure allows healthcare workers who were struck off their professional registers during the pandemic for serious violations connected to their anti-vaccination beliefs – for example, promoting treatments that lacked a scientific basis – to apply to be reinstated.

The bill is being championed by the prime minister Giorgia Meloni’s Brothers of Italy party and is strongly backed by its far-right coalition partner, the League. But with allies in Forza Italia split, its approval in the lower house hinged on support from National Future (FN), a rival far-right force led by the former army general Roberto Vannacci, whose emergence is shaping the political landscape before general elections next year. Vannacci has voiced opposition to vaccine mandates, and his rhetoric frequently targets the vaccine-sceptic audience.

blocks.caption: Roberto Vannacci, president of Futuro Nazionale, attends a rally in Milan on 2 November. Photograph: Alessandro Bremec/NurPhoto/Getty Images

blocks.text: The measure still needs to clear the senate, with a vote scheduled in January. But its progress has alarmed medical experts, less because of the number of healthcare workers involved – it is believed to be very small – and more because of the risk of further eroding trust in vaccines.

Nearly one in two Italian adults are hesitant about vaccination, according to a report by the department of public health and paediatric sciences at the University of Turin published in the Lancet Regional Health Europe in February. The report, which sampled 50,000 adults across Italy, found the ambivalence was driven more by misinformation and lack of institutional trust than by fears over vaccine safety.

“Political communication and the lack of trust among Italians in institutions carry a significant weight,” said Roberta Siliquini, the head of the school of hygiene and preventive medicine at the University of Turin and the report’s chief researcher. “There really is a disinformation campaign in this sense – and those who want to disinform are very good at communicating.”

The implications are being profoundly felt: this year there has been a resurgence in measles, with 472 infections reported during the first five months, compared with 322 in the same period last year, according to health ministry figures. More than half of the cases were reported in young adults. Take-up of the flu vaccine among people aged 65 and over so far this season has dipped to 49.81%, the first time it has fallen below 50% since the winter of 2014-15.

In August, a four-year-old child in Palermo, Sicily, died of diphtheria. Her parents reportedly told doctors they had not vaccinated her because her cousin was autistic and they were convinced vaccines were the reason. There is no evidence of any link between autism and vaccines.

blocks.caption: Demonstrators clash with police officers during a protest against the government’s introduction of the Covid ‘green pass’ in Rome on 9 October 2021. Photograph: Remo Casilli/Reuters

blocks.text: Siquilini said the tragic case was a reminder of the responsibility that everyone, “but especially politicians”, had to deliver the correct message on vaccines. He warned that the rehabilitation of those who rejected scientific evidence could have a “devastating” impact on how people perceived vaccines.
The message has been repeatedly undermined. On 28 October, a day after the lower house vote, Claudio Borghi, a League politician, came under fire for hosting an anti-vaccine seminar in the senate.

Later in the day, in what was believed to have been an indirect rebuke, the Italian president, Sergio Mattarella used a speech during a high-profile cancer research gathering to condemn the spread of anti-vax messages while warning against “irrational beliefs” and “destructive fake news”.

Borghi has proposed revising a law introduced in 2017 by the then leftwing government that extended the number of obligatory childhood vaccinations from four to 10, adding, for example, one against pertussis, or whooping cough. He has defended his position, arguing he is not anti-vaccine but that mandatory vaccines “lead to resistance”.

blocks.caption: A group protesting against the use of the green pass and the restrictions that were to come into effect for unvaccinated people in July 2021. Photograph: Lorenzo Palizzolo/Getty Images

blocks.text: As for the reinstatement of the medics struck off during the pandemic, he told the Guardian that the proposal’s aim was “to foster reconciliation after all these years”. He said: “In our view, nobody should lose their job because of a personal belief.”

Scepticism over vaccinations took root in Italy in the late 1990s, as in many other countries, mainly driven by now debunked claims of a connection between the combined measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccination and autism.

The arrival of social media accelerated the spread of vaccine misinformation, contributing to a drop in immunisation rates against preventable diseases. The 2017 move to make childhood vaccinations obligatory further emboldened anti-vaccine groups while creating fertile ground for rightwing populist parties, including the Five Star Movement (M5S), which continued to spread misinformation about vaccines after coming to power in 2018, and before the realities of the pandemic forced a shift in tone. Now in opposition, M5S is highly critical of the move to re-embrace anti-vax healthcare workers.
Lorenzo Mattia Signori, a nurse in Veneto, said politicians were “opportunists” and Meloni’s coalition was simply trying to draw votes from anti-vax voters as it eyed a second mandate.

Signori, who is also a regional secretary for Cittadinanzattiva, an association focused on patient advocacy, including pushing for campaigns to inform citizens about vaccine benefits, said: “Ensuring that people get vaccinated is the largest prevention system we have. If everyone gets sick instead, the Italian healthcare system would not hold.”

He hopes that Mattarella will use his power as president to stop the anti-vaccine medics measure from being signed into law. “We cannot have them in hospitals,” he said. “It would be like going to church and hearing a priest who says he doesn’t believe in God.”

articles.title: Palace defends P22.9-billion budget for 2026 ASEAN Summit
articles.summary: Malacañang defended the P22.9-billion budget for the 2026 ASEAN Summit, saying critics should focus on what the government has achieved rather than what it has spent.

blocks.text: November 12, 2026 | 6:17pm

(L-R) Myanmar's Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs U Hau Khan Sum, Malaysia's Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, Thailand's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, East Timor's Prime Minister Xanana Gusmao, Vietnam's Prime Minister Le Minh Hung, Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., Singapore's Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, Brunei's Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, Indonesia's President Prabowo Subianto, Cambodia's Prime Minister Hun Manet and Laos’ Prime Minister Sonexay Siphandone pose for a group photo during the opening ceremony of the 48th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in Cebu, central Philippines on May 8, 2026.
AFP / Aaron Favila / pool

MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Thursday, November 12, defended the P22.9-billion budget for the 2026 ASEAN Summit, saying critics should focus on what the government has achieved rather than what it has spent.

The allotment, Palace Press Officer Claire Castro explained, includes expenditures for the 48th ASEAN Summit held in Cebu in May 2026. The Philippines hosted the summit after Myanmar was skipped in the ASEAN chairmanship rotation due to the country's ongoing civil war.

Preparations for the 49th ASEAN Summit, meanwhile, include infrastructure improvements to the Philippine International Convention Center and World Trade Center in Pasay City, which will serve as the main venues for the event.

Renovations were also made to the Coconut Palace, a building located in the Cultural Center of the Philippines complex that was used as a guesthouse for prominent visitors during the term of former President Ferdinand Marcos Sr.

In terms of security, almost 20,000 police officers will be deployed across venues, hotels and motorcade routes during the event, along with additional personnel from the Armed Forces of the Philippines.
The 48th and 49th ASEAN Summits have brought around 550 policy meetings and working sessions to the Philippines, 393 of which have been completed.
The 2017 summit, Castro pointed out, had only 279.
Castro added that the government is ready to have summit expenses audited and to report how the budget was used.
Every peso spent, she said, is an investment in the country and in Filipino workers.
Labor group Sentro ng mga Nagkakaisa at Progresibong Manggagawa previously questioned the summit's toll on workers after various vendors were temporarily ordered to close to make way for the event.
Cash assistance was extended to 84 vendors in Pasay City and around 1,500 vendors in Parañaque City.

articles.title: British woman missing from cruise ship in Atlantic
articles.summary: The 72-year-old was last seen aboard the Tui ship on Monday as it headed towards the Caribbean.

blocks.text: A British woman has gone missing from a cruise ship while it was crossing the Atlantic, travel operator Tui has said.

The 72-year-old was last seen aboard Tui's Marella Voyager on Monday while the vessel was en route to the Caribbean. The ship could have travelled hundreds of miles in the time between when she was last seen to when she was reported missing.
Staff realised the passenger was missing on Tuesday, when they noticed her bed had not been slept in. The alarm was raised and a search carried out, Tui said in a statement.
It is understood the missing guest was then reported to the US Coast Guard, which asked the ship to continue to its crossing rather than reverse course and search for the woman.
Holidaymakers were told to abandon dinners, drinks and entertainment as the crew carried out an emergency headcount on Tuesday evening, the Daily Mail reports.
Passengers stood in lines of four while staff scanned boarding cards to verify the identity of every person on the ship, according to the newspaper.

The USCG Rescue Co-ordination Centre in Norfolk, Virginia has issued an alert calling on any ships nearby to "keep a sharp look out" for the woman, the Mail reports. The BBC has contacted the USCG for comment.

The Marella Voyager, carrying around 2,000 passengers and 800 crew, left Malaga on 4 November and is due to arrive in Antigua on Friday before calling at Dominica and finishing its voyage in Barbados on Sunday.
A spokeswoman for Marella Cruises said it was "deeply saddened" by the disappearance, adding: "Our thoughts are with the guest's loved ones at this very difficult time.
"We're supporting the authorities with their enquiries, and out of respect for the guest and their family, we won't be commenting further at this stage."
A UK Foreign Office spokesperson said: "We are supporting the family of a British national reported missing on a cruise ship in the Atlantic Ocean and we are in touch with the relevant authorities."
In a separate case, a cruise ship pianist was found treading water on Sunday around 20 miles off the Californian coast after falling overboard.

Two fishermen discovered the Royal Caribbean employee near Catalina Island and officials believe he may have been in the Pacific Ocean for nine hours, according to CBS News, the BBC's US news partner.

articles.title: US envoys arrive in Moscow for Ukraine talks with Vladimir Putin
articles.summary: Later on Thursday, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff will travel to Dublin to meet Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky.

blocks.text: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have arrived in Moscow for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, a day after the latest talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine wrapped up in Abu Dhabi.
Videos shared by Russian media showed Kushner and Witkoff disembarking a plane and being welcomed by Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev with handshakes and hugs.
The American negotiatiors were due to meet Putin at 12:00 local time (09:00 GMT), and will then fly to Dublin to speak to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
On Tuesday, Kushner said the US had seen "some openings and some opportunities" and that they would try to "make some progress" at the meeting with Putin.
The in-person talks with the Russian and Ukrainian presidents were only announced on Wednesday after two days of talks which were framed as centred around the postwar security architecture of Europe.

Nearly five years since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Moscow shows no sign of backing down from its maximalist demands for sovereign Ukrainian territory and for Western countries to give up any future commitment to protecting Kyiv in case of further attacks.
During the first years of the war, Europeans cut communicatons with the Kremlin and refused to engage with Russia directly.

However, in recent times many have grown concerned about the current US administration's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin, and have been pushing for a seat at the negotiating table.

The talks in Abu Dhabi were led by the Americans and only included Russia and Ukraine, but Kushner said he and Witkoff would ask Putin to "give his blessing" to invite European representatives in future discussions - particularly with regards to the future configuration of their continent's security architecture.
Kushner also urged Europe to "identify one person to speak on their behalf" in the negotiations.
But the Russians have been opposed to the idea, citing Europe's support for Kyiv as an obstacle.

Vladimir Medinsky, who headed the Russian delegation in Abu Dhabi, said he thought all parties had "moved closer to achieving peace" but that now "a lot depends on Ukraine, on the position of the United States, and on whether Europe comes to its senses".

As Witkoff and Kushner were meeting Russian officials in Moscow, Zelensky said Ukraine's military was again facing news of "systematic" restrictions to Starshield satellite internet, Elon Musk's SpaceX service which plays a key role for frontline communications. Connectivity issues in October lasted about a week. Musk denied deliberately throttling Ukraine's connection.
The restrictions have made it more difficult for Ukrainian forces to intercept Russian jet-powered drones, Zelensky said in a statement.
"This is helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes against Ukraine," he said.
"We are trying to clear up all circumstances with the American side."

articles.title: [READOUT] As Q3 GDP slows to 2.1%, what are businesses seeing?
articles.summary: Despite worsening economic figures, the country's biggest retailer and airline say demand is surprisingly resilient

blocks.text: The latest Philippine economic numbers paint a grim picture, with inflation rising, unemployment worsening, and economic growth slowing to its weakest pace since 2009, outside the pandemic.

But just as these figures were released, Rappler had the chance to speak with executives from some of the country’s biggest businesses about how they’re digesting the slowdown. Their responses suggest a more uneven picture, with some industries holding up better than others.
First, let’s recap the three big numbers:

items: Inflation rose 7.8% year on year in October, accelerating from 7.2% in September.
Unemployment climbed to 5.4% in September from 5.3% in August, leaving an estimated 2.86 million Filipinos unemployed.

The Philippine economy grew by just 2.1% in Q3 2026, down from 2.4% in the previous quarter and 4% a year earlier. This marked the weakest pace since 2009, excluding the pandemic years. Growth averaged only 2.5% in the first nine months of the year.

blocks.text: That leaves the Marcos administration on track to miss its annual growth target for the fourth year in a row. Economic growth would need to soar to 6.3% in the final quarter just to hit the lower end of its already reduced 3.5% to 4.5% target — a feat even the country’s chief economist admitted would be “very, very challenging.”
Department of Economy, Planning, and Development Secretary Arsenio Balisacan also warned that businesses should not expect consumer spending to recover quickly.
“I don’t expect consumer spending to rebound strongly soon,” he told reporters on November 9, citing the lingering effects of inflation.

Household consumption grew just 2.4% in the third quarter. BPI lead economist Emilio Neri Jr. pointed out that spending actually rose 8.5% in nominal terms, suggesting much of that went toward covering higher prices rather than buying more goods and services.
Nevertheless, two leaders of the SM Group didn’t seem too concerned about the latest macroeconomic numbers.

SM Supermalls president Steven Tan said mall foot traffic was still stable, with food-and-beverage sales even growing by double digits in October. Shoppers were also spending more time in malls, possibly consolidating trips as fuel prices rise.

But though retail remained strong, SM Prime president Jeffrey Lim acknowledged weaker residential demand and said the company would prioritize more stable income sources such as malls, hotels, and conventions.
“We’re not putting our expansion plans on hold. We are simply being more deliberate about how we spend,” Lim said.

Cebu Pacific is similarly seeing Filipinos continue to spend on travel, according to its president Xander Lao. Despite higher fuel costs and ticket prices, the airline expects to surpass last year’s record of 26.9 million passengers.
“Travel remains resilient regardless of the economic data that’s coming out,” Lao said.

Of course, these experiences do not erase the strain felt by consumers. A recent Organic Intelligence study found that 45% of surveyed urban Filipinos said inflation had drained their motivation to get ahead.
Meanwhile, Maharlika Investment Corporation president and CEO Joel Consing sees opportunities even amid the tough economic situation.
Speaking to reporters at the Fourth ASEAN Investment Forum, Consing said weaker economic growth could cause asset repricing and create attractive opportunities for investors to enter.

“We are not impacted by the weakness of GDP in terms of our investment strategy,” he said, explaining that Maharlika’s infrastructure investments address long-term needs regardless of short-term economic performance.
Consing also explained how the fund aims to invest in sectors where private companies may be reluctant to move first, eventually attracting more capital.
That need is pressing. Net foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows fell 23.9% in the first seven months of 2026 to $4.07 billion.

It’s no wonder then that after presenting the third quarter’s disappointing growth figures, Secretary Balisacan underscored that the Philippines needs more FDIs, not only for the money but also for the technology, expertise, and innovation foreign investors bring.
We hope this readout helps inform your next strategy or boardroom decision. And as always, feel free to tell us what to tackle next, dear business leader. – Rappler.com

Readout is a new content series from data consultancy The Nerve, bringing you insights that bridge the gap between quick news headlines and dense technical reports. Readout tracks and explains business shifts in different Philippine industries. Crafted from on-the-ground reporting and data-driven analyses, Readout provides a clear read on where market and consumption are headed, what’s shaping demand across different sectors, who the key players are, and why it all matters.

articles.title: Canada has the opportunity to become a global LNG leader, new report says
articles.summary: Canada’s only liquified natural gas facility began operating last year, yet the country has an opportunity to scale up that industry and become one of the top natural gas exporters in the world,…

image.caption: An LNG tanker in Kitimat, B.C., in April 2025. LNG Canada recently announced it would proceed with the second phase of the facility, which could double the amount of exports. (Maggie MacPherson/CBC)

blocks.text: Calgary

Canada’s only liquified natural gas facility began operating last year, yet the country has an opportunity to scale up that industry and become one of the top natural gas exporters in the world, according to a new report.
Larger LNG industry would make Canada less dependent on U.S., says energy expert

Canada’s only liquified natural gas (LNG) facility began operating last year, yet the country has an opportunity to scale up that industry and become one of the top natural gas exporters in the world, according to a new report.
There are several hurdles to overcome, though, including a lengthy permitting process and a lack of proposed projects by the private sector.
The federal government aims to grow LNG exports to upwards of 100 million tonnes per year.
Currently, one facility is operational with a capacity of 14 million tonnes per year.

Reaching the federal goal could have a significant economic impact, according to the report released Thursday by S&P Global, including nearly a quarter million jobs annually and nearly $1 trillion of investment in the natural gas industry by 2050.

“If Canada can address its permitting issues and its cost issues, Canada can play a very big role in global LNG, which would be obviously beneficial for the Canadian economy and would help to globalize its economy and make its economy less dependent upon on its neighbour to the south,” said Daniel Yergin, vice-chairman of S&P Global, in an interview with CBC News.

items: Canada is getting a second shot at becoming a major LNG player

blocks.text: Western Canada has a vast amount of natural gas, which can be produced at some of the lowest costs in North America.
However, building pipelines to transport the gas to the West Coast from Alberta and northeast B.C. has been a complex and expensive process.

The Coastal GasLink project, which was developed by TC Energy and is partly-owned by local First Nations, faced several delays and cost overruns. The project was opposed by various Indigenous communities and environmentalists. The pipeline project crosses about 625 lakes, rivers, creeks, wetlands and streams in northern B.C.

Some experts have said Canada will never be an LNG-exporting superpower because it has been so difficult to develop and construct energy infrastructure. There is also competition from many other countries that are wanting to attract LNG investment, including the U.S.

items: LNG could help break Canada's dependence on the U.S. energy economy — but there are no guarantees

blocks.text: Canada’s permitting process has taken 27 months longer compared to Texas, and pipelines cost 160 per cent more to build, according to the S&P report.
The federal government has introduced new legislation aimed at speeding up regulatory reviews.

LNG Canada is the only LNG export facility in the country, although six others are either under construction or in development. Altogether, they would produce just over 50 million tonnes of LNG each year.
S&P Global vice-chairman Daniel Yergin appears on stage at CERAWeek in Houston on March 10, 2025. Yergin says Canada has many advantages and hurdles to grow its LNG sector. (Kaylee Greenlee/Reuters)
One of the big secrets in the global energy industry is the size of Canada’s oil and natural gas, said Yergin, along with its geographical advantage of a relatively short shipping route to Asia.

“Asian buyers want that LNG from Canada,” said Yergin, along with other countries around the world, especially considering how the conflict in the Middle East this year has disrupted the global natural gas market. In Europe, there are concerns about the high cost of gas to heat homes as the winter months approach.

"There's a strong interest in diversification. There's a conviction that you have to build security and resilience into your system. You need a diversified portfolio, and it would be beneficial to have resources that don't have to go through choke points. And so all of those things point to advantages that Canada has right now,” he said.

items: Environmental group sends legal warning to pension funds over potential LNG investments

blocks.text: Prime Minister Mark Carney has a lot of credibility on the world stage, said Yergin, but investors will want to see proof of permitting reform since lengthy wait times can be very costly for companies.
Demand for natural gas is expected to grow over the coming decades due to a variety of factors, ranging from the world's growing population to power demand from AI data centres and air conditioning.
Canadian LNG has 55 per cent lower greenhouse gas intensity compared with similar projects in other countries, according to S&P Global.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Kyle Bakx is a Calgary-based journalist with the network business unit at CBC News. He files stories from across the country and internationally for web, radio, TV and social media platforms. You can email story ideas to kyle.bakx@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Halifax-area hospitals see pest control budgets soar amid mice, pigeon infestations
articles.summary: CBC News has learned that several Halifax-area hospitals have been dealing with soaring costs to deal with mice and pigeon infestations. Nova Scotia Health says it could take years to rid its…

image.caption: Jordan Bonaparte said this mouse was running around a family member's room in the emergency department at the Halifax Infirmary. He said the mouse was so brazen, it tried to climb into the bed to get to food. (Submitted by Jordan Bonaparte)

blocks.text: Nova Scotia·New

CBC News has learned that several Halifax-area hospitals have been dealing with soaring costs to deal with mice and pigeon infestations. Nova Scotia Health says it could take years to rid its facilities of the mice issue.
QEII hospital complex sees increase of 798% in pest control spending in 5 years
When Jordan Bonaparte went with a family member to the QEII Health Sciences Centre's emergency department in Halifax on Saturday, he was initially shocked to see mice scurrying around the halls.
But a paramedic quickly set him straight.
"One of them said there are as many mice as there are patients here, if not more," Bonaparte said. "My time in the Infirmary's emergency room definitely made that clear."
After watching mice for nearly six hours in the hall, he said his family member was moved to a room. Within minutes, he said, a mouse came out and started climbing on the bed with the patient.
"I'm pretty sure if I didn't get up and stomp my feet, that thing was going right up on my bed to get up where the food was that they were serving her," he said.
Nova Scotia Health is acknowledging that the issue at the QEII complex is beyond what is expected in a port city, where rodents are a common sight.
Documents obtained by CBC News reveal that the health authority's pest control bills at the QEII and Dartmouth General Hospital have soared in the last five years.
The QEII, which includes the Halifax Infirmary, Victoria General and Rehabilitation sites, saw its budget jump from $35,942 to $323,075. That's an increase of 798 per cent.
Dartmouth General saw the biggest percentage increase in the province in the same timeframe, going from $9,545 to $120,012 last year, an increase of 1,157 per cent.
"The volume of those sightings has increased exponentially over the last couple of years," said Chris Smith, the senior director for facilities operations at Nova Scotia Health.

"It's easy to say that we live in a port city and it's a thing, but it doesn't change our opinion and approaches that they don't belong in health-care settings and we've got to do whatever we can to keep them out and keep those environments clean, sanitary and safe."
Construction on the acute care tower at the QEII Health Sciences Centre has contributed to the rodent infestation, says Nova Scotia Health. (Build Nova Scotia)
Both sites are surrounded by extensive construction projects. Smith said when ground was broken on the QEII expansion project, he knew it would stir up the pests.
"We did expect an increase, but I don't think we expected quite the increase that we're seeing."

The health authority says in the last five years, it has caught 1,435 mice or other rodents in the QEII buildings, which cover 2.9 million square feet. A further 321 rodents have been nabbed at the Dartmouth hospital.

"We're in aging buildings and it's a complex environment. We've got hundreds of people, if not thousands, going in and out of the buildings every day for medical appointments, materials, supplies and equipment," Smith said.
The IWK Health Centre said it had to do extensive work to clean up a pigeon infestation. (Paul Palmeter/CBC)
The IWK Health Centre, meanwhile, said mice aren't its biggest issue, despite being next door to the QEII.
Last year, the women and children's hospital had to spend $180,000 after discovering "unusual bird activity," which was largely an issue with pigeons.
The IWK declined to do an interview, sending a statement instead.
"This included extensive cleanup of bird droppings and nesting areas, as well as applying netting and spiking in areas to deter birds in the future," the statement read.
The IWK said it expects to monitor the issue for a while, meaning some costs will be ongoing.
While the IWK cleanup is largely done, Nova Scotia Health is still in the thick of its infestation.
"It's a problem years in the making. It'll most likely take several years to fully get it under control," said Smith.

Smith said his department has a three-pronged approach. It has hired professional exterminators who visit every day, it's asking staff to report sightings so they know which areas to target with traps and they've started doing external inspections of the buildings, looking for small holes.
"Some of that effort resulted in 100 or 200 work orders for all of these little cracks and crevices that needed to be closed up," he explained.
"If there's any that are still open, we're actively working on them. It's not an overnight fix."
Smith is asking staff and patients to keep an eye out and report all sightings.
Days after Bonaparte visited the hospital, he's still shaken by his experience, and wants people to demand more of their facilities.
He posted a video of his experience to his podcast pages called The Canadian Gothic. The response included several comments of people saying it's normal.

"If your bar for health care is set so low that you're accepting there to be mice running around the emergency room where people are clinging to life, I think that's an unreasonably low expectation to have," he said.

articles.title: Ontario's moose population is in decline, and the province is trying to figure out why
articles.summary: The Ministry of Natural Resources and Forestry says strong predation numbers of wolves and black bears could be a major factor in moose decline while a conservationist says rising temperatures are…

image.caption: Predators, disease and vehicle collisions are all known causes of moose mortality in Ontario. But why the population hasn't recovered after two decades of decline remains unknown, according to the Ministry of Natural Resources and Forestry. (Amir Said/CBC)

blocks.text: Sudbury

The Ministry of Natural Resources and Forestry says strong predation numbers of wolves and black bears could be a major factor in moose decline while a conservationist says rising temperatures are putting stress on the large mammals.
Strong predation numbers could be major factor in moose decline while conservationist points to climate change

Since the early 2000s, the moose population in Ontario has dropped by about 20 per cent and upwards of 50 per cent in parts of the north — and the Ministry of Natural Resources and Forestry (MNRF) is trying to figure out why.
Ministry research scientist Nick Luymes recently hosted a presentation on the latest findings from his team’s multi-year moose research project in Wildlife Management Unit 13 near Thunder Bay.

Initiated in 2024, the project examines the various factors contributing to moose population decline, including predator-prey dynamics, pests and disease, calf survival, road impacts and forestry activities.
Despite significant reductions in hunting tags over the years, moose numbers have largely failed to increase in nearly two decades, according to Luymes.
“We want to get an understanding of what makes these limiting factors important so we can target that context in our manipulative experiments,” he said.
“We want any of our findings to be useful for other parts of the province and what’s driving those factors.”
Ministry research scientist Nick Luymes provides presentation on moose population study during the recent Northern Ontario Tourism Summit in Sault Ste. Marie. (Alex Flood/CBC)
What the ministry’s early findings suggest

In the last two years, biologists and technicians with the ministry have captured and collared more than 200 moose in the Thunder Bay area with GPS and video tracking to monitor their movements, behaviours and lifestyle.
“At capture, we get a lot of data such as pregnancy status, health, parasite load, condition of their body and information on genetics,” Luymes said.

Because of active predators like wolves and black bears, Luymes noted that much of the decline in moose can be attributed to low calf survival — with just one third of them making it through their first year.

items: Researchers search for answers to declining moose population in northwestern Ontario
Manitoba First Nation appeals to licensed moose hunters to turn tags in to province

blocks.text: His team determined the approximate annual survival rate for adult cows is 95 per cent and 70 per cent for adult bulls.
“We get alerts for when a moose might be dead. If they are, we can collect samples and do investigations at the site to understand why they died.”
To date, 36 of the ministry’s collared moose in the study area have died.
Vehicle collisions and hunting were the most common causes of mortality for adult males, while predation was the most common for calves and yearlings older than eight months.
For adult females, "unknown health problems" topped the list.
“We’re hoping to get better confirmation on what the specific causes are,” Luymes said.
“We have bodily samples submitted to labs that will do more formal analyses on what’s causing those deaths.”
A moose is collared as part of the ministry's ongoing study near Thunder Bay. (Ontario Fish and Wildlife)
Addressing predator concerns ‘a Band-Aid’ solution, says conservationist
Dave Pearce is a senior forest conservation manager with Wildlands League, a Toronto-based conservation group and partner with the Canadian Parks and Wilderness Society.
While he recognizes wolves and bears have certain implications on moose populations, Pearce isn’t convinced they should receive all the blame.
“It’s easy to say they’re driving things, so reduce the predator population,” he said. “But that’s kind of a Band-Aid that doesn’t really address the core fundamental issues.”
According to Pearce, a big contributor to stagnant moose numbers is climate change.
He points to rising and above seasonal temperatures as a key reason why the large mammals aren’t thriving like they used to.
“Especially in the spring, we’ve been having sudden onset of summer-like heat and moose can get hyperthermic and overheat very quickly,” he explained.
“Heat-stressed animals won’t move around and feed as much, and that doesn’t only impact the animal but its offspring too.”
Moose populations in Ontario are down despite there being fewer hunting tags than in previous years, according to the province. (CBC)
Pearce noted that a warming climate is beneficial to white-tailed deer. If their numbers go up, then more predators could flock to that habitat — ultimately impacting moose.
He also raised the issue of winter ticks that feed heavily on moose, though Luymes explained in his presentation that the ministry isn’t noticing any significant concerns of that in its study area.
During 10-day excursion last year, Sault hunter saw one moose
Jeremy Coulis has been hunting moose in northern Ontario since he was a young boy.
An Indigenous hunter from Batchewana First Nation and Sault Ste. Marie, Coulis also participates in the government regulated tag system with his non-Indigenous friends.
“It’s the social aspect and getting into nature,” he said. “Getting up with family and friends and getting away from technology for a few days. It’s nice.”
But in recent years, the sport has gotten much more challenging for Coulis and his group.
On a recent hunting trip this year just north of Aubrey Falls, he and seven of his friends saw four moose — three cows and one bull — during their week of hunting.
Last year, that same group only saw one moose there across 10 days of hunting.
“It’s definitely harder now,” he said. “You can spend days and days out there, but the moose just aren’t there.”
“When you see one, it’s actually kind of a shock and a surprise nowadays.”
Jeremy Coulis and his friends enjoy hunting for moose north of Aubrey Falls every fall. (Submitted by Jeremy Coulis)
With the decline in tags in recent years, Coulis has also noticed much fewer camps and hunters out in the bush.
When asked why he thinks moose numbers haven’t been recovering, Coulis expressed concerns over forestry companies that spray forests with herbicides.

Their goal in spraying is to kill broadleaf vegetation which competes with coniferous trees like spruce and pine that are harvested for their lumber — but environmentalists have voiced frustration with the practice in recent years.
“Quebec has proven that their moose population has rebounded substantially since they stopped spraying,” Coulis said. “But Ontario has no interest in stopping the spray.”
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

A College of Sports Media grad, Alex joined CBC News as a journalist in his hometown of Sault Ste. Marie in 2025. When he's not reporting, you'll find Alex cheering on the Canucks, playing piano and watching Schitt's Creek for the millionth time.

articles.title: Indonesia's vice-president resigns after academic credentials questioned
articles.summary: The Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled last month that the documents Gibran Rakabuming Raka submitted regarding his overseas education didn't meet election requirements.

image.caption: Gibran Rakabuming Raka leaves the parliament building in Jakarta on Thursday after submitting his resignation letter in Jakarta,. (Tatan Syuflana/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New
The Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled last month that the documents Gibran Rakabuming Raka submitted regarding his overseas education didn't meet election requirements.
Gibran Rakabuming Raka offered to resign during a meeting with President Prabowo Subianto
Indonesia's vice-president resigned Thursday as questions grew over his eligibility for the office after recent court rulings disputed his educational credentials.

Gibran Rakabuming Raka, the 39-year-old son of former president Joko Widodo, submitted his resignation to the leadership of the People's Consultative Assembly, the country's highest legislative body, at the parliament building in the capital, Jakarta.

Raka had offered to resign Tuesday during a meeting with President Prabowo Subianto, saying he wanted to avoid a prolonged political controversy. But a Cabinet minister said the president urged Raka at the time to defend himself and it wasn't clear if he accepted the resignation offer.
The Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled last month that the documents Raka submitted regarding his overseas education didn't meet election requirements.
A subsequent petition, submitted Wednesday to the House leadership by 120 lawmakers from eight political parties, began a parliamentary process that could lead to his impeachment.

Under Indonesian law, House leaders must establish a special committee to examine whether Raka has violated the constitution by serving as vice president, despite allegedly failing to meet election requirements.
If lawmakers determine there is sufficient basis for the accusation, the House must ask the Constitutional Court to rule on whether a constitutional violation has occurred.
The academic credentials investigation was apparently not related to investigations into allegations that top police officials had been involved in wiretapping targeting the president.

articles.title: Missing teen found alive after 6 days in the Australian woodlands
articles.summary: A 17-year-old boy with autism was found alive Thursday after six days lost in eastern Australian woodlands.

image.caption: In this image made from video and provided by the Victoria State Police 17-year-old William, centre right, is embraced by his mother Elizabeth, only first names were provided by police, while in a helicopter in Cowwarr, Australia, Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026, after William spent six days lost in eastern

blocks.text: World·New
A 17-year-old boy with autism was found alive Thursday after six days lost in eastern Australian woodlands.
The boy had begun camping with a teenage friend when he disappeared

The boy, whom police identified only as William, had begun camping with a teenage friend when he disappeared last Friday near Walhalla, a former gold-mining town 185 kilometres east of Melbourne, police said.

A police helicopter crew found him surrounded by wilderness lying asleep on a flat rock beside a creek, and he was later reunited with his mother. William was in good spirits and mostly in good health, the police statement said.
Video shot from the rescue helicopter showed he was shirtless and sunburned. He was wearing shorts and boots and was using towels as blankets.
"I'm just over the moon that he's alive," his mother, Elizabeth, told reporters. The AP has decided not to provide her family name to avoid identifying her son.
"And he's never leaving the house again. He's grounded for life. He's not going anywhere ever again," she joked.
William was later taken to a hospital for his health to be monitored, police said.
William's family have said he has Level 2 autism. That requires "substantial support," according to the Australian advocacy group Autism360.
Such a person may have marked deficits in verbal and non-verbal social communication and rely heavily on routines and predictable activities. Disruption can cause significant distress.
The Southern Hemisphere spring weather had been mild for the past week in the alpine region where William was lost and there had been little rain.

Elizabeth had dropped off her son and his friend last Friday for a weekend of camping. William walked a short distance from the campsite to the drop-off location to collect more camping equipment but never returned to his friend, police said.
After becoming lost, William trekked for days up and down "some very steep terrain," Acting Police Inspector Jason Benbow said.
He spent the last two days where he was found at the creek, trapped by the steepness of his surrounds 2 kilometres from the his camp site, Benbow said.
"He woke up to the sound of the helicopter, gave them a thumbs up and they winched him to safety," Benbow told reporters.
The extensive police search for him involved more than 100 emergency services personnel and volunteers.

blocks.text: Here's a roundup of news from or pertaining to Germany on November 12, 2026:
November 12, 2026
Police raid sites of Gremium MC biker gang in Baden-Württemberg

blocks.caption: Police launched operations across the southwestern state early on ThursdayImage: Bernd Weißbrod/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Hundreds of police officers searched apartments and meeting sites for the biker group "Gremium MC" in the southwestern state of Baden-Württemberg early on Thursday.

The state interior ministry said the operation was part of a move to outlaw three sub-chapters of the group, the ones based in Böblingen and Leonberg, as well as the "Gremium MC Chapter Nomads Bosphorus Türkiye."

This last group was highlighted as a meaningful part of Gremium MC by security officials. It describes itself on Facebook as a great example that "people of different cultures and faiths can be strong together," featuring images of men posing with knives and other weapons.

Gremium MC prominently incorporates into its iconography the symbol of the Prussian military medal for exceptional valor, the Iron Cross, which was discontinued after World War I, reintroduced by Adolf Hitler during World War II, and then scrapped for good.
State Interior Minister Manuel Hagel was expected to make further comments later in the day in Ludwigsburg.

Gremium MC is deemed an "outlaw motorcycle gang" in Baden-Württemberg's latest security report, a term used for biker groups that do not recognize the state monopoly on the use of force and are often tied to organized crime.
"Extortion, drug dealing and pimping in particular tend to be part of their activities," state authorities say.
Baden-Württemberg counts 154 biker chapters in the state with around 2,000 members.

Founded in 1972 in Mannheim, various chapters of Gremium MC across the country have faced legal issues in recent years. In 2021, another chapter in the southwest, Gremium MC Southgate in Heidelberg, was outlawed on suspicion of organized crime activity.

articles.title: DOJ launches 'Sure Ka Na Ba?' campaign vs. online scams
articles.summary: The Department of Justice (DOJ) on Thursday launched a public awareness campaign to help Filipinos recognize and avoid online scams amid the increasing number of people exposed to fraudulent schemes.

blocks.text: Published November 12, 2026 5:43pm
The Department of Justice (DOJ) on Thursday launched a public awareness campaign to help Filipinos recognize and avoid online scams amid the increasing number of people exposed to fraudulent schemes.

According to a report by Darlene Cay on GTV's Balitanghali, the "Sure Ka Na Ba?" public awareness campaign against cyber scams aims to enable Filipinos to identify suspicious messages, calls, and links before they become victims.
"We aim to equip every Filipino with the knowledge and practical skills to recognize the warning signs of an online scam," Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida said.

"We want every Filipino to learn how to spot a scam, understand how it works, report suspicious incidents, and empower others to protect themselves. In other words, I want their 'sure ka na ba' to be 'sure na.' This is the preventive approach," he added.
About 84% of Filipino adults encountered scams in the past year, higher than the 77% recorded in 2025, based on the 2026 State of Scams in the Philippines report of the Global Anti-Scam Alliance.
Under the DOJ campaign, the word "SURE" represents four steps that the public should remember when dealing with potential scams:

items: Spot — Identify whether a message, call, or link could be a scam
Understand — Learn how scams work and how to protect oneself
Report — Immediately report suspected scams to the appropriate authorities
Empower — Help others avoid falling victim to fraudulent schemes

blocks.text: Vida said Filipinos should make it a habit to ask themselves, "Sure ka na ba? (Are you sure?)" before clicking suspicious links, sending money, or engaging with questionable offers.
The DOJ chief stressed that while the department continues to strengthen efforts to hold scammers accountable and build cases against them, it also wants to empower the public to protect themselves.
Vida also shared that he had been used in an impersonation scam, recounting that someone recently called an acquaintance and pretended to be him to solicit money.
Filipinos who encounter suspicious messages or fall victim to scams may report the incidents to authorities, their respective banks, or e-wallet providers.
They may also send reports to the DOJ through cybercrime@doj.gov.ph.
— VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Australian teen found alive after six days in the bush
articles.summary: The teenager was spotted during an aerial search, after spending days navigating rugged terrain. He had fallen down the side of a riverbed two days before being found.

image.caption: 'I'm just over the moon he's alive,' William's mother was quoted in Australian media as sayingImage: Victoria Police/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: An Australianteenager has been found alive after six days missing in dense bushland.

Police said 17-year-old William had been camping with a friend in the southeastern state of Victoria, about 180 kilometers (112 miles) east of Melbourne. He got lost after he'd left his friend to go and get some equipment, but didn't return.
The friend then called the police and an intense search operation was launched, involving helicopters, special units, as well as volunteers searching the bush each day.

The boy was found on Thursday morning during an aerial search near Stoney Creek, public broadcaster ABC reported. Rescuers first spotted a fishing tackle box and then saw the boy sleeping on a rock in a dry riverbed.
'In good spirits and good health'
Pictures show the boy shirtless and sunburned. Local media reported that he waved and pumped his fist when he was woken up the sound of the search helicopter.

"Flight officers winched down and retrieved Will before bringing him back to the command post to reunite with his mum," police said. "Amazingly, William is in good spirits and for the most part, in good health."
He was then taken to hospital for monitoring.
"I'm just over the moon he's alive," his mother was quoted in Australian media. "He just stayed in one spot and waited to be rescued."
Police said William had spent days walking through the rugged terrain but fell down the side of a riverbed two days ago and then remained there in hopes of being found.
"He's never leaving the house again," his mother told local reporters. "He's grounded for life."

blocks.text: Ukraine faces 'systemic speed restrictions' on Starshield again that 'help Russians kill more Ukrainians', Zelenskyy says
Oh-oh.
Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelenskyy has just taken to X to say that the Ukrainian army is once again experiencing “significant disruptions to Starshield’s operations over the territory of Ukraine.”
He said the problem has been going on “for several days now,” affecting operations “along the entire frontline and in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine.”

“Specifically, systematic speed restrictions are being imposed on Starshield, limiting it to 161 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour). The Ukrainian military have already investigated the circumstances, and these are not random errors but systematic speed restrictions.”

Spelling out the real life consequences, Zelenskyy said the disruption complicates intercepting Russian jet-powered drones, with “strikes that got through because our interception systems cannot reach sufficient speeds and are unable to intercept in time.”
“Unfortunately, this is helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes against Ukraine. We are trying to establish all the circumstances with the American side.”

blocks.text: Bomb alert at Calais-Fréthun train station causes delays on domestic, cross channel services
I am also keeping one eye on another bomb alert in Europe, this time at Calais-Fréthun station in northern France.

“Due to a request for police assistance at Calais-Fréthun, your train is delayed. We’re waiting for more information and we’ll confirm your estimated delay as soon as possible. Thanks for your patience.”
I will let you know if and when we know more.
EU to approve new sanctions on Russia on Monday, France's Europe minister says
Meanwhile, the EU is planning to approve new sanctions on Russia on Monday, France’s Europe minister Benjamin Haddad said.

“On Monday, we will take new sanctions against Russia, on 150 additional entities, 50 ⁠banks and it’s France which proposed the bulk of the entities to add,” Haddad told LCI ⁠television, as reported by Reuters.
“We will continue to put economic pressure on Russia ​and of course support Ukraine,” ‌he added.

blocks.caption: France's junior minister in charge of Europe Benjamin Haddad speaks at an event this week. Photograph: Ludovic Marin/AFP/Getty Images
Jakub Krupa

blocks.text: Jakub Krupa

US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are in Moscow this morning, where they are expected to meet Russia’s president Vladimir Putin to advance some of the issues discussed at trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi over the last two days.

The meeting is expected to get under way around 9am GMT, with Russia’s deputy foreign minister Sergei Rybakov trying to manage everyone’s expectations by saying it was too early to say that necessary trust had been restored between Russia and Ukraine.

blocks.text: The US envoys are then expected to fly to Dublin to meet Volodymyr Zelenskyy on the margins of the European Political Community summit, which is being attended by more than 40 leaders from Ukraine’s allied countries.
The EPC – set up on the initiative of France’s Emmanuel Macron – offers a rare chance to discuss key European issues with non-EU allies, including Britain’s Andy Burnham and Canada’s Mark Carney.

blocks.caption: Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Ireland's taoiseach Micheál Martin attend a bilateral press conference at Government Buildings, in Dublin, Ireland last night. Photograph: Cathal McNaughton/Reuters

blocks.text: For Burnham, it’s also an opportunity to dot the i’s and cross the t’s ahead of next week’s EU-UK summit, which is a key part of his proposed reset in relationship with the bloc. Let’s see what we are going to hear on this today.
For Dublin, the meeting comes with a massive security operation, particularly after some past concerns about drones, particularly around Zelenskyy’s visit to Ireland last December.
I will keep an eye on both of these events and bring you all the latest here.
It’s Thursday, 12 November 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.
Good morning.

articles.title: LinkedIn, Monster take down over 1,000 fake job postings after CBC investigation
articles.summary: More than 1,500 misleading job postings on LinkedIn and Monster were actually connected to a multi-level marketing company, a CBC News visual investigation has found.
articles.byline: Eric Szeto, Courteney Dorrington, Jordan Pearson, Ivan Angelovski

image.caption: Hundreds of job postings posted to LinkedIn and Monster actually brought applicants into the recruiting process for a multi-level marketing company, a CBC News visual investigation has found. (Illustration: Matthew Hoddy/CBC, LinkedIn, Monster, Soho A Studio)

blocks.text: More than 1,500 misleading job postings — offering remote work, no experience needed — have been taken down from LinkedIn and Monster after a CBC visual investigation revealed the listings funnelled unsuspecting applicants to a multi-level marketing (MLM) company that asked for money.

CBC connected a network of travel-related pages posting suspicious jobs — positions like "Work From Home Travel Planner and Virtual Customer Support Representative" — to a U.S.-based MLM called Evolution Travel. Some of the roles promised to pay up to $75,000 US per year.
In reality, there was no job and no salary.

Applicants were quickly directed to join virtual information sessions, where they were asked to pay hundreds of dollars up front, followed by a monthly subscription fee. The program promised to teach members how to make money from booking travel as an independent agent and recruiting others into the program, taking a cut of their commissions.
Exposing who’s behind fake job ads online
The companies went by names like Wanderwell Collective, Professional Travel Hub, Remote-Careers, Sky Land & Ocean Travel and Sunkissed Getaways.
The job postings made no mention of Evolution Travel or sign-up fees.
Many of the jobs did not require experience and promised to pay up to $75,000 US. (Illustration: Matthew Hoddy/CBC; LinkedIn)

"This is disgusting," said Jay Jones, a Chicago-based job listing investigator who CBC shared its findings with. "They catch you with the lure of the fake job. The money is great, [successful applicants] get to stay at home. You have to pay to get work — that's not how work works."
Misleading job postings — including ones that require payment or lead to MLMs — are strictly prohibited on platforms like LinkedIn and other job sites.
Jay Jones investigates misleading and fake jobs online. (CBC)

"It feels in so many ways that we're living in a funhouse mirror," said Vass Bednar, managing director of the Canadian Shield Institute, a public policy think-tank that focuses on economic resilience and digital sovereignty.
These postings risk "eroding confidence — confidence in the self and confidence that there is, frankly, meaningful work out there for people that is worth pursuing."
Jobs were 'misleading': LinkedIn

MLMs are not illegal in Canada or the U.S. However, in the U.S., companies and individuals could face fines if they are found to violate the U.S. Federal Trade Commission Act, which prohibits "unfair or deceptive acts or practices in or affecting commerce."

"I would consider [these job posts] misleading… and would invite enforcement by either the FTC, the state governments or other federal enforcement agencies," said William Kovacic, former FTC chairman and commissioner, with whom CBC also shared its findings.

One independent agent behind multiple travel businesses linked to misleading jobs ads CBC identified — Wanderwell Collective, Destination Knot, Aisle and Abroad, and Professional Travel Hub — was Diedre Norton. In one video posted to YouTube, Norton said she had a network of 300 recruits for Evolution Travel.
Even though Evolution Travel’s founder, David McCovy, praised her in online videos as being a top performer, Norton denied being affiliated with the program before hanging up on CBC News.
Screenshot of an online video showing Evolution founder David McCovy during a conference. (EvolutionTravelCafe/YouTube)
McCovy did not respond to CBC’s requests for comment.

A representative from Evolution Travel who only identified themselves by their title, chief operating officer, told CBC they have consistently told their independent agents not to post job ads on any platforms.

Late last month, LinkedIn took down close to 900 ads connected to Evolution Travel, saying it had removed them because they were "misleading and violated" company policy, adding "the companies behind them will no longer be able to post jobs" on the platform.

Monster took down 600 listings, saying it has "clear policies prohibiting misleading job postings and multi-level marketing opportunities, and we take action to remove listings that do not meet our standards."

Hundreds of job postings posted to LinkedIn and Monster actually brought applicants into the recruiting process for a multi-level marketing company, a CBC News visual investigation has found. (Illustration: Matthew Hoddy/CBC, LinkedIn, Monster)
Detecting fake jobs
Evolution Travel does not operate in Canada, but CBC journalists still came across the job posting in their feeds. They were also recommended in emails from LinkedIn.
The ads contained immediate red flags. The travel companies named in the ads had minimal to no presence online, and there were close to 1,500 postings, often with almost identical job descriptions.
Many of the jobs did not require experience and were remote. CBC found more than 1,500 misleading or fake jobs. (LinkedIn)
The jobs, in many cases, required no education, no prior experience and often did not require a resumé.

CBC applied for eight jobs on LinkedIn and Monster, attaching a blank document as a resumé in cases that required it. Upon applying, the team was sent automated emails to join a virtual information session by individuals connected to Evolution Travel.
CBC journalists were sent automated emails and asked to join a virtual information session by individuals connected to Evolution Travel upon applying for the jobs. (CBC)
Evolution Travel and its partner Archer Travel Services describe themselves as an international "home-based travel business" that trains its members to book travel and earn a commission.

But it's not just about booking travel. Archer Travel’s website describes Evolution Travel as its "recruiting partner" and describes it as a "network marketing" company — another term for multi-level marketing, according to the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

A compensation plan for members on Evolution Travel’s website shows a percentage of commissions and monthly bonuses are paid to the most effective recruiters, with membership tiers up to "8 Star Platinum" for recruiting 100,000 people.
Documents show compensation plans for Evolution Travel. (Evolution Travel)

None of this was mentioned in the information sessions CBC attended, which covered travel booking exclusively. When a CBC journalist posing as a job applicant asked about getting commissions from their own recruits, the session host said it was not covered in the information sessions and that the person who invited them into the program would address it.
Session hosts also didn’t disclose there is a hidden $50 annual fee in the independent contractor agreement, seen by CBC, when signing up.
A screenshot from an Evolution virtual session shows the packages attendees can pay to enrol in the program. (Evolution Travel)
Former FTC chairman and commissioner Kovacic said if he were still at the agency, he would be looking into the company.
"[Fees are] not presented in the initial interaction," he said. "It's shrouded in a way that's very important and would mislead users."
27,000 independent contractors
Job seekers have been complaining about Evolution Travel, its members and agents like Deidre Norton online and to the Better Business Bureau for years.

In 2021, Evolution Travel was among 1,000 companies put on notice by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission that they could face fines if they or their representatives made "misleading, or deceptive representations" about a "money-making opportunity."
Kovacic said a firm that "defied" FTC notices and continued to persist in these practices would be a "worthy target for an investigation."
CBC News found numerous complaints online about companies linked to the job postings. (Illustration: Matthew Hoddy/CBC, Reddit, Better Business Bureau)
Ron Archer, the CEO of Archer Travel Services, said that the company does "not condone illegal job postings and addresses them when we are made aware."
Yet in videos online, travel agents connected to Evolution Travel talked openly about using LinkedIn job postings to recruit people into the business.
Archer said they cannot "tell people how they train for their business" because they have "27,000 independent contractors around the world."
"LinkedIn is a big one," said one member in a June 2026 training video posted to YouTube. "We have quite a few different trainings on how to post on LinkedIn."
Jay Jones, who has gotten tens of thousands of jobs taken down from platforms himself, said companies like LinkedIn and Monster generate revenue through this traffic.

"There's no actual vetting of what companies get to be created, what jobs get to be listed," said Jones. "People coming [to LinkedIn] believing that there are real opportunities are greeted with this MLM nonsense."
